editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the physics (S_1/S_2 expansions, |<S>| <= 2, Tsirelson bound, "63/64 pairs violated", "peaks fall short because of device noise") all survives intact, no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims, and the informal register holds with no po/opo. What a native editor would still change is a layer of calques and two dropped/shifted qualifiers. Calques: "bold curves" -> "matapang na kurba" (brave, not makapal/bold), "traces the same sinusoid" -> "sumusubaybay" (monitors), "If you found this work interesting" -> "Kung nahanap mong kawili-wili" (nahanap = located), "we tile the backend" -> "inuulit ang backend" (repeats), "exercised end-to-end" -> "masanay nang buo" (gets accustomed), "Finally" -> "Sa wakas" (at last). Qualifier slips: the Nobel sentence drops "in part" ("iginawad ... dahil sa kanilang pioneering work"), "experimentally test Bell's theorem" is strengthened to "eksperimentong patunayan" (prove), and "qualitatively similar to what we expect from hardware" becomes "kalidad na katulad" (similar in quality), a slightly stronger claim than the English. Also within-file spelling split "teorama ni Bell" vs "teoremang ito" in the same paragraph, and "Background" rendered as "Pinagmulan" (origin) where "Panimula/Kaligiran" is the section convention. None of these would leave a learner with a false belief about CHSH.

examples.source: The 2022 Nobel Prize for Physics was awarded to Alain Aspect, John Clauser, and Anton Zeilinger in part for their pioneering work in quantum information science
examples.translation: Ang 2022 Nobel Prize for Physics ay iginawad kina Alain Aspect, John Clauser, at Anton Zeilinger dahil sa kanilang pioneering work sa quantum information science
examples.suggested: ... ay iginawad ... dahil, sa bahagi, sa kanilang pioneering work sa quantum information science
examples.why: "in part" is dropped, so the Tagalog reads as if the prize was awarded solely for that work. A dropped qualifier, not a technical distortion.

examples.source: is used to experimentally test Bell's theorem (1969)
examples.translation: ay ginagamit upang eksperimentong patunayan ang teorama ni Bell (1969)
examples.suggested: ay ginagamit upang eksperimentong subukin ang teorema ni Bell (1969)
examples.why: "patunayan" = prove, which strengthens "test". Same sentence also spells it "teorama" while the next sentence uses "teoremang ito" — an in-file inconsistency.

examples.source: the bold curves are their mean across the device
examples.translation: ang mga matapang na kurba ay ang kanilang average sa buong device
examples.suggested: ang mga makapal na kurba ay ang kanilang average sa buong device
examples.why: "matapang" is "brave/strong-flavored"; the typographic sense of bold is "makapal". A literal-word calque a native technical writer would never use for a plot line.

examples.source: transpile against the simulator's target so the same pass manager is exercised end-to-end
examples.translation: ini-transpile laban sa target ng simulator upang ang parehong pass manager ay masanay nang buo
examples.suggested: ini-transpile gamit ang target ng simulator upang ang parehong pass manager ang magamit mula simula hanggang dulo
examples.why: "laban sa" literalizes "against" as combat, and "masanay" (get accustomed) mistranslates "exercised" (put through its paces). Reads as machine output; the intent is still recoverable.

examples.source: Here we tile the backend with as many disjoint Bell pairs as its connectivity allows
examples.translation: Dito natin inuulit ang backend na may maraming disjoint Bell pair hangga't pinapayagan ng connectivity nito
examples.suggested: Dito natin binabalot/tinatakpan ang backend ng kasindaming disjoint Bell pair hangga't pinapayagan ng connectivity nito
examples.why: "inuulit ang backend" (we repeat the backend) loses the tiling image; the rest of the clause still carries "as many as connectivity allows", so the paragraph does not mislead.

examples.source: We measure the second qubit in the Z and X bases.
examples.translation: Susukat tayo ng pangalawang qubit sa $Z$ at $X$ bases.
examples.suggested: Susukatin natin ang pangalawang qubit sa $Z$ at $X$ bases.
examples.why: The indefinite "Susukat tayo ng" reads as "we will measure a second qubit" rather than "the second qubit"; the definite "Susukatin natin ang" is what a native writer would use here.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim tracks the English (monitoring ~once an hour interleaved with user jobs, calibrations only on the qubits/gates flagged, "wala pang dalawang oras bawat araw" for under two hours, the queue-pause behavior, and the Admonition's device-drift caveat all survive intact), and the informal register holds with no po/opo. The main defect is lexical: the verb for "monitor" is rendered as the non-word "sinisimoni" / "sumusimoni" (lines 10, 18, 28), an invented affixation no Tagalog technical writer would produce — the file's own "subaybayan"/"minomonitor" is the natural choice, and it sits inconsistently beside the correct "subaybayan ang mga parameter" in the same sentence on line 10. Smaller slips: "kumikillos" is a typo for "kumikilos" (line 21); "mga katanggap-tanggap na hanay" uses "hanay" (row/array) where "saklaw" is the term for a numeric range, and the same sentence has the redundant "sinusuri upang suriin"; and a few English-shaped calques remain ("ang IBM na fleet ng mga quantum computer" line 10, "alinman nang programatiko o sa pahina" line 65). Domain terms themselves are handled well and consistently — qubit, gate, readout, fidelity, crosstalk, coherence time, and calibration are kept in English throughout with Tagalog grammar wrapped around them.

examples.source: IBM quantum computers are frequently monitored to track parameters that may drift over time
examples.translation: madalas na sinisimoni ang mga IBM quantum computer upang subaybayan ang mga parameter na maaaring lumihis
examples.suggested: madalas na minomonitor ang mga IBM quantum computer upang subaybayan ang mga parameter na maaaring lumihis
examples.why: "sinisimoni" (and "sumusimoni" on line 28) is not a Tagalog word — it is a garbled affixation of "monitor". Native usage is "minomonitor" or "binabantayan"; the file already uses correct "subaybayan" in the same clause, so the reader meets two renderings of the same idea side by side.

examples.source: to check whether any parameters have begun to deviate from acceptable ranges
examples.translation: ay sinusuri upang suriin kung ang anumang parameter ay nagsimulang lumihis mula sa mga katanggap-tanggap na hanay
examples.suggested: ay sinusuri upang matukoy kung may parameter nang nagsimulang lumihis sa mga katanggap-tanggap na saklaw
examples.why: "hanay" means row/column/array, not a numeric range — "saklaw" is the conventional term. The same sentence also repeats the stem in "sinusuri upang suriin", which reads as machine output rather than edited prose.

examples.source: confirming they behave as expected
examples.translation: na nagkukumpirma na ang mga ito ay kumikillos ayon sa inaasahan
examples.suggested: na nagpapatunay na kumikilos ang mga ito ayon sa inaasahan
examples.why: "kumikillos" is a straightforward typo for "kumikilos" — a native editor would not ship it in a published guide.

examples.source: the IBM fleet of quantum computers ... either programmatically or on the Compute resources page
examples.translation: ang IBM na fleet ng mga quantum computer ... alinman nang programatiko o sa pahina ng Compute resources
examples.suggested: ang fleet ng mga IBM quantum computer ... sa pamamagitan ng programa o sa pahina ng Compute resources
examples.why: Both are English-shaped calques: "IBM na fleet" forces an English noun into a Tagalog ligature slot, and "alinman nang programatiko o" is a word-for-word mapping of "either … or" that Tagalog handles with a bare "o".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: "merely a collection of one or more passes" keeps its hedge ("isang koleksyon lamang"), the conductor/orchestra analogy survives intact, and "Higher levels generate more optimized circuits at the expense of longer transpilation times" is rendered correctly as "mas na-optimize na mga circuit ngunit mas matagal ang transpilation." The defects are naturalness/consistency only. "Generate" is rendered two ways within the file — "makabuo" (generate_preset_pass_manager paragraph) but "Nagbubunga" in the Default transpilation section, where "nagbubunga" (to bear fruit / yield) reads odd for a function that generates and runs a StagedPassManager. "will inject gates (that is, SWAPs)" is calqued as "mag-iiniksyon ng mga gate" (medical injection), and "In addition to reducing…" uses the malformed nominalization "pagbababa" where the same idea earlier used "nagpapababa". "Submitting a job" flattens to "nagpapadala ng trabaho", losing the Qiskit sense of `job`. None of these would teach a learner anything false.

examples.source: This generates and runs one of the preset `StagedPassManager` objects
examples.translation: Nagbubunga at nagpapatakbo ito ng isa sa mga preset na object na `StagedPassManager`
examples.suggested: Bumubuo at nagpapatakbo ito ng isa sa mga preset na object na `StagedPassManager`
examples.why: "Nagbubunga" means to bear fruit/yield; for code that generates an object a native technical writer uses "bumubuo". Line 47 already renders generate as "makabuo", so the file is inconsistent with itself.

examples.source: will inject gates (that is, SWAPs) in the original circuit
examples.translation: mag-iiniksyon ng mga gate (iyon ay, SWAPs) sa orihinal na circuit
examples.suggested: magpapasok ng mga gate (iyon ay, mga SWAP) sa orihinal na circuit
examples.why: "Mag-iiniksyon" is the medical sense of inject; it is a direct calque no Tagalog-speaking engineer would write for inserting gates into a circuit.

examples.source: In addition to reducing the depth and complexity of quantum circuits
examples.translation: Bukod sa pagbababa ng depth at complexity ng mga quantum circuit
examples.suggested: Bukod sa pagpapababa ng depth at complexity ng mga quantum circuit
examples.why: "Pagbababa" (unloading/lowering something physically) is the wrong nominalization here; the causative "pagpapababa" matches the verb "nagpapababa" already used for the same idea in the preceding section.

examples.source: When submitting a job to an IBM Quantum® backend
examples.translation: Kapag nagpapadala ng trabaho sa isang IBM Quantum® backend
examples.suggested: Kapag nagsusumite ng job sa isang IBM Quantum® backend
examples.why: `job` is a Qiskit Runtime object, not generic "work"; "trabaho" also collides with the earlier "utility-scale na trabaho", blurring two different senses.

editor_note: The technical spine is faithful — constant/balanced conditions, the 2^n/2+1 worst case, the exponential-vs-deterministic / no-speedup-vs-probabilistic contrast, and the all-zeros=constant readout all survive intact — but two prose sentences in the last 40% break down. The coin-flip analogy in the "100% certainty" answer is rendered as "Parang paulit-ulit na pagpupukpok ng barya at laging lupalop" ("like repeatedly *hammering* a coin and always *a far-flung region*"): "pukpok" is not tossing and "lupalop" is not "heads", so the intuition the English builds (a long run of identical outcomes is unlikely but possible) is destroyed, and the follow-up leaves "Unlikely" untranslated. Worse, the B-V comprehension question turns "How does this help us understand how the same algorithm solves two different problems?" into "Paano nito **tinatalunan** kung paano nireresolved..." — "tinatalunan" reads as disputing/defeating, i.e. the opposite of the guiding intent the learner is supposed to follow. Also: the verb "solve" is split between correct "niresolba" (line 579) and the malformed hybrid "nireresolved" (lines 637, 643, 647), "satisfies" appears as the non-word "nagsasatisfy", and "The code below will generate a balanced function 50% of the time" becomes "magrerehistro" (will *register*) instead of "gagawa/bubuo".

examples.source: It's like flipping a coin over and over and it landing heads every time. It's unlikely, but not impossible.
examples.translation: Parang paulit-ulit na pagpupukpok ng barya at laging lupalop. Unlikely, pero posible.
examples.suggested: Parang paulit-ulit na paghagis ng barya at laging ulo ang lumalabas. Malabong mangyari, pero hindi imposible.
examples.why: "pagpupukpok" means pounding/hammering, not tossing, and "lupalop" (a far-flung region) is not "heads" — the analogy that carries the whole worst-case intuition is meaningless in Tagalog. "Unlikely" is also left in English.

examples.source: How does this help us understand how the same algorithm solves two different problems?
examples.translation: Paano nito tinatalunan kung paano nireresolved ng parehong algorithm ang dalawang magkaibang problema?
examples.suggested: Paano nito tinutulungan tayong maunawaan kung paano nireresolba ng parehong algorithm ang dalawang magkaibang problema?
examples.why: "tinatalunan" reads as disputing/arguing over (or defeating), which reverses the pedagogical thrust of "help us understand" — the learner is told the observation undercuts the point instead of explaining it.

examples.source: solves / satisfies
examples.translation: "niresolba" (579) vs "nireresolved" (637, 643, 647); "nagsasatisfy" (577, 637, 643)
examples.suggested: Consistently "nireresolba"/"nilulutas"; "tumutugon sa"/"natutugunan ang" for satisfies.
examples.why: "nireresolved" glues a Tagalog affix onto an English past participle and is not a word; the same verb is rendered two ways within one section.

examples.source: The code below will generate a balanced function 50% of the time, and a constant function 50% of the time.
examples.translation: Ang code sa ibaba ay magrerehistro ng balanced na function 50% ng pagkakataon...
examples.suggested: Ang code sa ibaba ay gagawa/bubuo ng balanced na function sa 50% ng pagkakataon...
examples.why: "magrerehistro" means "will register/record", not "will generate" — it misdescribes what dj_function() does.

examples.source: extracting as much information as possible in a single run is a subtle art / ... by testing it experimentally / ... simplifies to
examples.translation: ...ay isang malikhaing sining / ...nang eksperimentalmente / Lumalabas na ang estado sa itaas ay simplipikahin sa
examples.suggested: ...ay isang pinong sining; ...sa pamamagitan ng eksperimento; ...ay nagiging simple lang na
examples.why: "malikhaing sining" (creative art) loses "subtle"; "eksperimentalmente" is a Spanish-style adverb no Tagalog technical writer uses; "ay simplipikahin sa" is an ungrammatical passive calque of "simplifies to".

editor_note: No semantic drift, dropped caveats, or hallucinated claims: every prose paragraph tracks the English, including the tricky AQC narrative at line 184 ("Una, isang target state ang binubuo... Sa wakas, ang resulta ay pinagsama sa natitirang mga Trotter step") and the dry-run caveat at line 337, and domain terms (Hamiltonian, ansatz, observable, expectation values, backend, ini-transpile) are kept in English consistently with informal register throughout. What a native technical editor would still fix are calques and word-form slips: "time evolution ... laban sa isang user-defined spin-based Hamiltonian" (line 14) calques "against" into the adversarial "laban sa" where Tagalog wants "sa ilalim ng"; "Sumusunod ay isang simpleng halimbawa" (line 136) is a word-order calque of "Following is a simple example" instead of "Narito ang isang simpleng halimbawa"; and "gaano karami ang gusto mong i-compress" (line 52) renders degree ("how much") as quantity ("how many"). There are also three small form errors: the heading verb "Pangolektahin" (line 50) is not a standard Tagalog form (should be "Kolektahin"), "nagbababalik" (line 150) is an over-reduplicated "nagbabalik", and "metadata na nabuong sa proseso" (line 393) leaves the linker "-ng" dangling. Additionally "actionable information" is flattened to the generic "kapaki-pakinabang" (line 539), the same word used for plain "useful" ten lines later, so the English's stronger claim is slightly softened — none of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: simulate the time evolution of an initial state against a user defined spin-based Hamiltonian
examples.translation: pag-simulate ng time evolution ng isang initial state laban sa isang user-defined spin-based Hamiltonian
examples.suggested: pag-simulate ng time evolution ng isang initial state sa ilalim ng isang user-defined spin-based Hamiltonian
examples.why: "laban sa" is the adversarial "against" (versus/opposing) and is a direct calque; Tagalog expresses evolution under a Hamiltonian with "sa ilalim ng" or "ayon sa". Meaning survives but the phrasing reads as MT.

examples.source: Following is a simple example of printing the `estimator_options`...
examples.translation: Sumusunod ay isang simpleng halimbawa ng pag-print ng `estimator_options`...
examples.suggested: Narito ang isang simpleng halimbawa ng pag-print ng `estimator_options`...
examples.why: Fronting "Sumusunod ay" copies English word order; no Tagalog technical writer opens a sentence that way — the idiomatic presentative is "Narito ang".

examples.source: such as how much you want to compress the initial layers of the Trotter circuit using AQC-Tensor
examples.translation: tulad ng kung gaano karami ang gusto mong i-compress ang mga initial layer ng Trotter circuit gamit ang AQC-Tensor
examples.suggested: tulad ng kung gaano kalaki ang gusto mong i-compress ang mga initial layer ng Trotter circuit gamit ang AQC-Tensor
examples.why: "gaano karami" asks "how many" (count); the source asks about degree of compression, which Tagalog marks with "gaano kalaki"/"gaano kahigpit". A quantity/degree mismatch, though not enough to mislead.

examples.source: ### Collect and validate the inputs
examples.translation: ### Pangolektahin at i-validate ang mga input
examples.suggested: ### Kolektahin at i-validate ang mga input
examples.why: "Pangolektahin" is not a well-formed Tagalog verb; the object-focus imperative of "kolekta" is "Kolektahin" (or actor-focus "Mangolekta"). It also clashes with the correctly-formed "i-validate" beside it.

examples.source: These can provide actionable information about the progress of the Hamiltonian simulation workflow.
examples.translation: Makapagbibigay ito ng kapaki-pakinabang na impormasyon tungkol sa progreso ng Hamiltonian simulation workflow.
examples.suggested: Makapagbibigay ito ng impormasyong maaari mong pagbatayan ng aksyon tungkol sa progreso ng Hamiltonian simulation workflow.
examples.why: "actionable" is flattened to the generic "kapaki-pakinabang" (useful) — the same word then used for plain "useful metadata" at line 549, so the English's stronger point (the logs let you decide what to do next) is softened.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the four job statuses (QUEUED/INITIALIZING/RUNNING/DONE), the "30 random circuits" figure (faithful to the source's own mismatch with the code), and the queue-priority and workloads-table caveats all survive intact, and register stays casual throughout. The defects are grammatical/naturalness: the ability construction is inverted twice in the status list — "maaari kang makuha ng mga logs" and "maaari kang makuha ng data na naka-store", where the actor-focus verb is required ("maaari kang kumuha ng..." / "maaari mong makuha ang..."); as written the reader is grammatically the thing being obtained. Similarly "Matagumpay mong natakbo ang iyong unang Qiskit Serverless program" uses the wrong verb form (should be "napatakbo"), and in the tip block the imperative "find release notes" is flattened to the non-imperative "makita ang mga release notes" while "is getting an upgrade" is softened to the vaguer "nagbabago". None of these would teach a learner a false fact, but a native technical editor would rewrite all four.

examples.source: you can retrieve logs using `job.logs()` / you can retrieve data stored in `save_result()`
examples.translation: maaari kang makuha ng mga logs gamit ang `job.logs()` / maaari kang makuha ng data na naka-store sa `save_result()`
examples.suggested: maaari kang kumuha ng mga logs gamit ang `job.logs()` / maaari mong makuha ang data na naka-store sa `save_result()`
examples.why: "maaari kang makuha" puts the reader in the object-focus slot — grammatically it reads as 'you can be retrieved'. The actor-focus 'kumuha' (or 'maaari mong makuha ang') is what a native writer would use. Occurs twice in the same status list.

examples.source: You've successfully run your first Qiskit Serverless program!
examples.translation: Matagumpay mong natakbo ang iyong unang Qiskit Serverless program!
examples.suggested: Matagumpay mong napatakbo ang iyong unang Qiskit Serverless program!
examples.why: 'natakbo' is the wrong verb form here (it reads as 'ran over / was run through'); the causative 'napatakbo' is the correct and idiomatic form, and it matches 'Patakbuhin' used in the title and headings of this same file.

examples.source: **Qiskit Serverless is getting an upgrade, and its features are changing fast.** During this development phase, find release notes and the most recent documentation at ...
examples.translation: **Ang Qiskit Serverless ay nagbabago at mabilis na nag-e-evolve ang mga feature nito.** Sa panahon ng development phase na ito, makita ang mga release notes at pinakabagong dokumentasyon sa ...
examples.suggested: **May paparating na upgrade ang Qiskit Serverless, at mabilis na nagbabago ang mga feature nito.** Sa panahon ng development phase na ito, hanapin ang mga release notes at pinakabagong dokumentasyon sa ...
examples.why: 'is getting an upgrade' is flattened to the generic 'nagbabago', losing the specific claim; and the English imperative 'find' is rendered as the non-imperative 'makita' ('to see/be seen') instead of the directive 'hanapin' / 'tingnan', so the tip stops instructing the reader.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the load-bearing details all survive intact (resilience levels 0-2 with the Level 1/Level 2 table, "hindi sinusuportahan ng Estimator V2 ang resilience level 3" plus the PEC/`pec_mitigation` caveat, the (4,1)×(1,6)→(4,6) broadcasting example, "hatiin ang mga count sa bilang ng shots"), and no hallucinated claims appear. What a native editor would still change: "Sampler V2 is simplified" is rendered "Ang Sampler V2 ay pinahusay" (= enhanced/improved), which reports the wrong kind of change even though the "makatutok sa pangunahing gawain nito" clause preserves the point; "without weights" is calqued as "nang walang mga timbang" (physical weight) instead of keeping "weights"/"hindi tinimbang"; and "at the cost of exponential processing time" is calqued as "sa halaga ng exponential na oras" where Tagalog wants "kapalit ng". There is also a nonstandard "na mag-aaplai sa lahat ng PUB" (Sampler step 5) where the parallel Estimator step 5 correctly says "na ilalapat sa lahat ng PUB", plus the parallel Estimator/Sampler migration steps drift apart ("Pagsamahin" vs "Pangkatin", "gumawa ng mga update ayon sa pagkakailangan" vs "gumawa ng mga pagbabago kung kinakailangan"). Register is consistently casual — no po/opo.

examples.source: Sampler V2 is simplified to focus on its core task of sampling the output register from execution of quantum circuits.
examples.translation: Ang Sampler V2 ay pinahusay para makatutok sa pangunahing gawain nito na pag-sample ng output register mula sa pagpapatupad ng mga quantum circuit.
examples.suggested: Ang Sampler V2 ay pinasimple para makatutok sa pangunahing gawain nito...
examples.why: 'pinahusay' means improved/enhanced, not simplified — it reports a different kind of change than the source. The following clause keeps the intent, so a learner is not left with a false API belief, but the claim is altered.

examples.source: It returns the samples, whose type is defined by the program, without weights.
examples.translation: Ibinabalik nito ang mga sample, ang uri nito ay tinukoy ng programa, nang walang mga timbang.
examples.suggested: ...nang walang weights (hindi tinimbang).
examples.why: 'timbang' is physical weight in Tagalog; as a rendering of statistical 'weights' it is a literal calque no Tagalog-speaking quantum engineer would write. Compare 'unweighted na sample' kept in English later in the same file.

examples.source: You can optionally specify `shots` here, which would apply to all PUBs.
examples.translation: Maaari kang opsyonal na tukuyin ang `shots` dito, na mag-aaplai sa lahat ng PUB.
examples.suggested: ...na ilalapat sa lahat ng PUB.
examples.why: 'mag-aaplai' is a nonstandard hispanized coinage; the parallel Estimator step 5 (line ~507) already uses the correct 'na ilalapat sa lahat ng PUB', so the file contradicts itself on the same sentence.

examples.source: ...which is proven to give unbiased results at the cost of exponential processing time.
examples.translation: ...na napatunayang nagbibigay ng unbiased na mga resulta sa halaga ng exponential na oras ng pagpoproseso.
examples.suggested: ...kapalit ng exponential na oras ng pagpoproseso.
examples.why: 'sa halaga ng' is a word-for-word calque of 'at the cost of' and reads as a monetary price; Tagalog uses 'kapalit ng' for a tradeoff.

examples.source: Review all the supported options and make updates accordingly. / Group each circuit you want to run...
examples.translation: Estimator: 'gumawa ng mga update ayon sa pagkakailangan' / 'Pagsamahin ang bawat Circuit'; Sampler: 'gumawa ng mga pagbabago kung kinakailangan' / 'Pangkatin ang bawat circuit'
examples.suggested: Use one rendering for each verb across the two parallel step lists.
examples.why: The Estimator and Sampler migration steps are deliberately parallel in the English; rendering the same instructions two different ways makes them look like different procedures on a skim.

editor_note: The upgrade caution box inverts a navigation instruction: English "skip ahead to the [Install and set up](#local) section" becomes "laktawan ang seksyong [I-install at i-set up](#local)", which in Tagalog reads as "skip/omit the Install and set up section" — the exact opposite advice for a first-time installer, who is being told to bypass the very instructions they need ("dumiretso sa seksyong…" is the correct rendering). A second, smaller drift is in the Compilation-errors accordion, where "which in turn might require some extra dependencies" loses its hedge and becomes the flat assertion "na nangangailangan naman ng ilang karagdagang dependency". Beyond those, a few native-editor fixes: "Whether you will work locally or in a cloud environment" is rendered as "Kahit magtatrabaho ka nang lokal o…" (reads as "even if" rather than "whether… or"), "Qiskit depends on…" as "Umaasa ang Qiskit sa…" (hopes/relies rather than "nakadepende sa"), and "corrupted somewhere along the way" as "masira… sa pagbabago", which does not correspond to the English adverbial. Everything else — the OS tier tables, pip/venv steps, Tier 1/2/3 wording — is faithful and consistently phrased.

examples.source: (If you are installing Qiskit for the first time, skip ahead to the [Install and set up](#local) section.
examples.translation: (Kung ito ang unang beses mong nag-i-install ng Qiskit, laktawan ang seksyong [I-install at i-set up](#local).
examples.suggested: (Kung ito ang unang beses mong mag-i-install ng Qiskit, dumiretso ka na sa seksyong [I-install at i-set up](#local).
examples.why: 'Laktawan ang seksyon' means skip/omit that section. The English sends the first-time user TO that section; the Tagalog tells them to bypass the install instructions — an inverted directive that misleads exactly the reader the caveat is aimed at.

examples.source: which in turn might require some extra dependencies that need to be installed manually.
examples.translation: na nangangailangan naman ng ilang karagdagang dependency na kailangang i-install nang manu-mano.
examples.suggested: na maaaring mangailangan naman ng ilang karagdagang dependency na kailangang i-install nang manu-mano.
examples.why: The modal 'might' is dropped, turning a possibility into a stated requirement — the same paragraph correctly keeps 'maaaring' elsewhere, so the hedge loss is inconsistent as well as stronger than the source.

examples.source: Whether you will work locally or in a cloud environment, the first step for all users is to install Qiskit.
examples.translation: Kahit magtatrabaho ka nang lokal o sa cloud environment, ang unang hakbang…
examples.suggested: Lokal ka man magtrabaho o sa cloud environment, ang unang hakbang…
examples.why: 'Kahit … o …' reads as 'even if', a calque of the English 'whether'; the idiomatic Tagalog correlative is '…man … o …'. Meaning survives but the opening sentence reads as machine output.

examples.source: Qiskit depends on a number of other open-source Python packages
examples.translation: Umaasa ang Qiskit sa ilang ibang open-source na Python package
examples.suggested: Nakadepende ang Qiskit sa ilang ibang open-source na Python package
examples.why: 'Umaasa' carries the sense of hoping/counting on rather than technical dependency; a Tagalog technical writer would use 'nakadepende sa', which matches the 'dependency' terminology used a few lines later in the same paragraph.

examples.source: if your Python environment becomes corrupted somewhere along the way
examples.translation: kung masira ang iyong Python environment sa pagbabago
examples.suggested: kung masira ang iyong Python environment sa kalagitnaan ng trabaho mo
examples.why: 'Sa pagbabago' ('in the change') does not render 'somewhere along the way' and leaves the clause slightly incoherent, blunting the intuition the sidebar is trying to teach about disposable environments.

editor_note: No misleading content: the packaging narrative (metapackage → single `qiskit` distribution, `qiskit-terra` frozen on PyPI, namespace hooks removed in v1.0) is faithful, the informal register holds throughout with no po/opo, and packaging jargon (module, package, distribution, namespace package, search path, requirement) is consistently kept in English as the glossary intends. What a native technical editor would fix is a cluster of ungrammatical/calqued spots: "Mahistoriko" is not the Tagalog for "Historically" (should be "Sa kasaysayan" / "Noong una"), and the repeated "ilang ngayon ay-obsolete na mga package" hyphenates English into a broken Tagalog phrase. Two sentences are grammatically broken enough to blur direction of dependency: "iba pang mga distribution na umaasa ito" (the required "dito"/"na inaasahan nito" marker is missing, so it can read as "distributions that depend on IT" — the reverse of the English), and "walang isang distribution ... ang kinakailangan may-ari ng lahat ng naka-install na file". Also "Nagbigay ito ng babala sa nito" (should be "dito"), "eksakto isang package" (needs "eksaktong"), and "pinaka-hindi-nagkakamaling istraktura" for "least error-prone" — all stiff-but-parseable, none rising to a FAIL.

examples.source: Historically, Qiskit was comprised of many Python distributions
examples.translation: Mahistoriko, ang Qiskit ay binubuo ng maraming Python distribution
examples.suggested: Sa kasaysayan, binubuo ang Qiskit ng maraming Python distribution
examples.why: "Mahistoriko" is not an adverb a Tagalog technical writer would produce for "historically" — it is a coined calque; the idiomatic openers are "Sa kasaysayan" or "Noong una pa." The same paragraph also reads "ilang ngayon ay-obsolete na mga package," a hyphenated English graft that should be "ilang package na obsolete na ngayon."

examples.source: A distribution contains information on other distributions it depends on when installed.
examples.translation: Ang isang distribution ay naglalaman ng impormasyon tungkol sa iba pang mga distribution na umaasa ito kapag naka-install.
examples.suggested: Naglalaman ang isang distribution ng impormasyon tungkol sa iba pang distribution na inaasahan nito kapag naka-install.
examples.why: "na umaasa ito" is missing the linker/pronoun that fixes who depends on whom; as written it can be parsed as "other distributions that depend on it," which reverses the dependency direction the glossary entry is defining. The next sentence rescues it, so this stays minor rather than misleading.

examples.source: Critically, no one distribution contributing to a namespace package necessarily owns all the installed files
examples.translation: Mahalaga, walang isang distribution na nag-aambag sa isang namespace package ang kinakailangan may-ari ng lahat ng naka-install na file
examples.suggested: Mahalagang tandaan: walang iisang distribution na nag-aambag sa isang namespace package ang tiyak na nagmamay-ari ng lahat ng naka-install na file
examples.why: "ang kinakailangan may-ari" is not a well-formed Tagalog predicate — the adverbial "necessarily" was dropped in as a bare adjective. The point (no single contributor owns everything) still comes across, but the sentence reads as raw MT.

examples.source: we will leave its most recent version in a working state, so old scientific code and legacy packages can more easily continue to use it
examples.translation: iiwanan namin ang pinakabagong bersyon nito sa isang gumaganang estado, para mas madaling magpatuloy na gamitin ang lumang scientific code at legacy package
examples.why: The agent/patient roles flip: in English the old code and legacy packages are the ones that keep USING qiskit-terra; the Tagalog reads as though the old code and legacy packages are the things being used. The practical takeaway survives, so this is a stiffness/role-marking slip, not a FAIL — but "para mas madaling magpatuloy na gamitin ito ng lumang scientific code at legacy package" is what a native editor would write.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every conditional survives intact ("Hindi ito pinapansin kung tinukoy na ang `instance`" for "This is ignored if `instance` is specified", "Kung manu-mano mong tinukoy ang iyong mga credential, hindi gagamitin ang na-save na account", "Kung isa lang ang account na iyong na-save, awtomatiko itong itinakda bilang default"), no dropped caveat, no invented claim, and the register stays casual (iyong/mo, no po/opo). What a native editor would still change: (1) the last Next-steps bullet replaces the English link label "Run your first circuit on hardware" with a bare "[Hello world]", losing the descriptive cue that tells the learner what the guide does; (2) the modifier "specific" is left untranslated in the headings/examples ("isang specific na instance", "mga specific na instance") while the same idea is rendered natively as "partikular" in the `plans_preference` bullet — an inconsistency inside one file; (3) a few calqued openers read like MT rather than a Tagalog engineer's prose, notably "Kung nagtatrabaho ka sa isang trusted na Python environment" and "Siguraduhin na nagtatrabaho ka sa isang aktibong Python environment", where a native writer would use "kung gumagamit ka ng" / "tiyaking nasa aktibong Python environment ka". None of these mislead.

examples.source: Follow the steps in the [Run your first circuit on hardware](/guides/hello-world) guide to write and run a quantum program.
examples.translation: Sundin ang mga hakbang sa [Hello world](/guides/hello-world) para magsulat at magpatakbo ng quantum program.
examples.suggested: Sundin ang mga hakbang sa gabay na [Patakbuhin ang iyong unang circuit sa hardware](/guides/hello-world) para magsulat at magpatakbo ng quantum program.
examples.why: The link label was swapped for the page's old title, so the bullet no longer tells the reader what the guide covers (running a first circuit on hardware). Informational loss, not a false statement.

examples.source: a specific instance / specific instances vs. a certain plan type
examples.translation: isang specific na instance / mga specific na instance vs. isang partikular na uri ng plano
examples.suggested: Use "partikular" consistently: "isang partikular na instance", "mga partikular na instance".
examples.why: The same modifier is rendered as untranslated English in two places and as native Tagalog in a third within one short file; a single convention should hold.

examples.source: If you are working in a trusted Python environment ... / Ensure you are working in an active Python environment ...
examples.translation: Kung nagtatrabaho ka sa isang trusted na Python environment ... / Siguraduhin na nagtatrabaho ka sa isang aktibong Python environment ...
examples.suggested: Kung gumagamit ka ng trusted na Python environment ... / Tiyaking nasa aktibong Python environment ka ...
examples.why: "nagtatrabaho ka sa" is a word-for-word calque of "working in"; in Tagalog it evokes employment rather than operating inside a runtime environment, and reads as machine translation to a native technical reader.

editor_note: The 15 August 2024 entry inverts what the `noise-learner` helper does: "It allows characterizing the noise processes affecting the gates" becomes "Nagbibigay-daan ito sa pagpapakilala ng mga proseso ng ingay na nakakaapekto sa mga gate" — "pagpapakilala" means *introducing*, so a learner reads that the helper injects noise into the gates rather than characterizing/learning it; the same file renders "characterization" correctly as "pagsasalarawan" later (Q-CTRL/QEDMA entry), so it is also inconsistent. A second false-friend inverts a product statement: "We will eventually sunset IBM Quantum Platform classic" becomes "Susunugin namin sa huli ang IBM Quantum Platform classic" ("we will burn it"). Smaller defects: "novel reactive fluids" → "mga nobelang reactive fluid" (nobela = the book genre, not "new"); "This update benefits users…" → "Ang update na ito ay nakikinabang sa mga user" reverses who benefits; "usability" → "kagalingan" (excellence); plus the typos "Ibinabaod" (for Ibinubuod, IBM Quantum Platform intro) and "sinasasakripisyo", and the calque "Nagsasalita ang mga resulta para sa kanilang sarili". Register is correctly casual throughout with no po/opo, and numbers/dates/QPU names all check out.

examples.source: It allows characterizing the noise processes affecting the gates in one or more circuits of interest, based on the Pauli-Lindblad noise model.
examples.translation: Nagbibigay-daan ito sa pagpapakilala ng mga proseso ng ingay na nakakaapekto sa mga gate sa isa o higit pang mga circuit ng interes, batay sa Pauli-Lindblad noise model.
examples.suggested: Nagbibigay-daan ito sa pagsasalarawan (characterization) ng mga proseso ng ingay na nakakaapekto sa mga gate sa isa o higit pang circuit na interesado ka, batay sa Pauli-Lindblad noise model.
examples.why: 'Pagpapakilala' = introducing/presenting, not characterizing. As written, the noise-learner appears to ADD noise to the gates — the opposite of its function — and the learner forms a false concept of noise learning. The file itself uses the right word ('pagsasalarawan') for 'characterization' in the QEDMA bullet.

examples.source: We will eventually sunset IBM Quantum Platform classic, so stay tuned for updates.
examples.translation: Susunugin namin sa huli ang IBM Quantum Platform classic, kaya abangan ang mga update.
examples.suggested: Sa kalaunan ay ititigil/ireretiro namin ang IBM Quantum Platform classic, kaya abangan ang mga update.
examples.why: 'Susunugin' literally means 'we will burn'. It is a false-friend rendering of 'sunset' and states an action IBM is not taking; the intended meaning (retire/discontinue the service) is lost.

examples.source: ...to study the dynamics of novel reactive fluids developed to transfer heat more efficiently...
examples.translation: ...para pag-aralan ang dynamics ng mga nobelang reactive fluid na binuo para mas mahusay na maglipat ng init...
examples.suggested: ...para pag-aralan ang dynamics ng mga bagong uri ng reactive fluid na binuo para mas mahusay na maglipat ng init...
examples.why: 'Nobela' in Tagalog is the literary novel; the adjective 'novel' (= new) is 'bago' or 'makabago'. The phrase reads as 'novelistic fluids' and misstates the fact that these are newly developed fluids.

examples.source: This update benefits users who manage multiple instances or prefer a streamlined workflow...
examples.translation: Ang update na ito ay nakikinabang sa mga user na namamahala ng maraming instance o mas gustong gumamit ng streamlined na workflow...
examples.suggested: Nakikinabang sa update na ito ang mga user na namamahala ng maraming instance o mas gustong gumamit ng streamlined na workflow...
examples.why: 'Nakikinabang' takes the beneficiary as subject, so the Tagalog says the update benefits FROM the users — the roles are swapped relative to the English.

examples.source: This section summarizes... / The results speak for themselves... / improvements in speed, quality, and usability
examples.translation: Ibinabaod ng seksyong ito... / Nagsasalita ang mga resulta para sa kanilang sarili... / mga pagpapabuti sa bilis, kalidad, at kagalingan
examples.suggested: Ibinubuod ng seksyong ito... / Kitang-kita na sa mga resulta ang pagbuti... / mga pagpapabuti sa bilis, kalidad, at kadalian ng paggamit
examples.why: 'Ibinabaod' is a typo for 'Ibinubuod'; 'Nagsasalita ang mga resulta para sa kanilang sarili' is a word-for-word calque no Tagalog technical writer would use; 'kagalingan' means excellence, not usability, so the third item duplicates 'kalidad' instead of naming ease of use.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful end-to-end — the cost-limit definition ("palaging magiging mas malaki o katumbas ng kabuuang gastos"), the currency-fluctuation caveat, the "*pagkatapos* lumampas ang gastos" trigger ordering, and the hourly-billing/multi-day-invoicing delays all say exactly what the English says, and register stays informal throughout. Three copy-edit level slips remain: a typo "itatatakda" for "itatakda" in the cost-limit-reached section; the calqued tail "kailangang gamitin kasama ang iba pang mga paraan ng pamamahala ng gastos sa ilang dahilan", where "sa ilang dahilan" reads as a literal carry-over of "for several reasons" instead of "dahil sa ilang kadahilanan"; and the UI label "Actions menu" translated as "menu ng Mga Aksyon" while every neighboring UI string (**Edit details**, **Save changes**, "overflow menu", "Total cost limit") is correctly left in English, so the reader is told to look for a control that is not labeled that way on screen. None of these would mislead a learner about how cost limits work.

examples.source: Its status is set to Canceled with a reason of Ran too long.
examples.translation: Ang status nito ay itatatakda sa Canceled na may dahilang Ran too long.
examples.suggested: Ang status nito ay itatakda sa Canceled na may dahilang Ran too long.
examples.why: "itatatakda" is a misspelling of the future form "itatakda" (extra syllable); a native technical editor would fix it on sight.

examples.source: IBM Cloud spending notifications must be used with other methods of cost management for several reasons:
examples.translation: Ang mga notification sa paggastos ng IBM Cloud ay kailangang gamitin kasama ang iba pang mga paraan ng pamamahala ng gastos sa ilang dahilan:
examples.suggested: Kailangang gamitin ang mga notification sa paggastos ng IBM Cloud kasabay ng iba pang paraan ng pamamahala ng gastos dahil sa ilang kadahilanan:
examples.why: "sa ilang dahilan" is a word-for-word calque of "for several reasons" and does not work as a Tagalog adjunct here; the passive-fronted clause is also stiffer than a native writer would put it.

examples.source: click the Actions menu at the end of the row, and then click **Edit details**
examples.translation: i-click ang menu ng Mga Aksyon sa dulo ng row, pagkatapos ay i-click ang **Edit details**
examples.suggested: i-click ang Actions menu sa dulo ng row, pagkatapos ay i-click ang **Edit details**
examples.why: The interface is English, and the same file keeps every other on-screen label untranslated (Edit details, Save changes, Total cost limit, overflow menu). Translating only this one label makes the instruction inconsistent with what the user actually sees.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the technically load-bearing sentences all survive intact — the $2^N$ by $2^M$ → "awtomatikong ipinapalagay na M-qubit at N-qubit" mapping keeps M/N in the right order, the "hindi mahahati sa mga qubit subsystem → single-qubit operator" condition is not inverted, the exponential-memory caveat and the "kabaligtaran ng hugis ng pinagbabatayan na matrix" tuple note are both preserved, and the register stays informal (no po/opo). What a native editor would still change is small: (1) "store" is rendered inconsistently — "nag-iimbak"/"mag-imbak" in the Operator intro and the `data` bullet, but "itatabi" (set aside/put away) for the same English verb in the $6\times6$ paragraph, where "iimbak" is the right word for storing data; (2) the lead paragraph's "Ipinaliwanag sa natitirang bahagi ng page na ito…" uses perfective aspect ("explained") where the English is present-tense "explains" — should be "Ipinapaliwanag ng natitirang bahagi…", which also fixes the missing ng-marker; (3) "pagkuha ng adjoint" for "determining its adjoint" softens to "getting" and is out of step with the parallel "pagtukoy kung ito ay (anti)commutes" in the same sentence. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: then it will be stored as a single-qubit operator
examples.translation: ito ay itatabi bilang isang single-qubit operator
examples.suggested: ito ay iimbak bilang isang single-qubit operator
examples.why: Elsewhere in the file the same English verb 'store' is rendered with imbak ("nag-iimbak ng linear operator", "mag-imbak ng dense matrix"). 'Itatabi' means to set aside / put away and is not the idiomatic word for storing data, so the file splits one term two ways.

examples.source: The rest of this page explains how to use `SparsePauliOp` and other operator classes.
examples.translation: Ipinaliwanag sa natitirang bahagi ng page na ito kung paano gamitin ang `SparsePauliOp` at iba pang mga klase ng operator.
examples.suggested: Ipinapaliwanag ng natitirang bahagi ng page na ito kung paano gamitin ang `SparsePauliOp` at iba pang mga klase ng operator.
examples.why: Perfective 'Ipinaliwanag' reads as past tense where the English is a present-tense signpost, and the sa-marker makes the rest-of-page a location rather than the agent; a Tagalog technical writer would use the imperfective with ng.

examples.source: such as determining its adjoint, whether it (anti)commutes with another `Pauli`
examples.translation: tulad ng pagkuha ng adjoint, pagtukoy kung ito ay (anti)commutes sa isa pang `Pauli`
examples.suggested: tulad ng pagtukoy ng adjoint nito, kung ito ay (anti)commutes sa isa pang `Pauli`
examples.why: The English governs both items with one verb ('determining'); the translation swaps the first to 'pagkuha' (getting/obtaining) while keeping 'pagtukoy' for the second, breaking the parallel list and slightly weakening the sense.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout the load-bearing parts — the shots precedence list, the "hindi tinukoy ng anumang PUB ... ang halaga ng shots mula sa mga opsyon ang gagamitin" fallback, and the twirling admonition ("mabibigo ang trabaho kung ... mas maliit kaysa sa halaga ng `shots`") all preserve the English conditions, quantities and caveats intact, and the compatibility accordions keep every "ngunit sa mga gate lamang na hindi nasa loob ng mga conditional block" qualifier. The one real weak spot is "Isinusulat nito ang anumang halagang itinakda para sa `default_shots`" for "This overwrites any value set for `default_shots`" — "isinusulat" is just "writes", so the override relationship is muddled (it should be "Ino-o-override/Pinapalitan nito"); the precedence is restated correctly further down, so it confuses rather than teaches a false rule. Otherwise the slips are stylistic: "initializing/initialized" is rendered as "sinisimulan ... masimulan ang Sampler" (= "starting/begun", not the technical "i-initialize"), "Limits how long a job can run" comes out in the past tense as "Nilimitahan ang tagal ..." instead of "Nililimitahan", and `run()` is attached two ways in adjacent paragraphs ("`run()` na pamamaraan" vs. the natural "pamamaraang `run()`"). Register is consistently casual with no po/opo, and domain terms (shots, PUB, twirling, backend, gate/circuit/Qubit, transpiled) are kept in English consistently.

examples.source: This overwrites any value set for `default_shots` for the current run.
examples.translation: Isinusulat nito ang anumang halagang itinakda para sa `default_shots` para sa kasalukuyang run.
examples.suggested: Ino-override nito (pinapalitan) ang anumang halagang itinakda para sa `default_shots` para sa kasalukuyang run.
examples.why: "Isinusulat" = "writes", dropping the "over-" that carries the whole point: the run() value supersedes default_shots. As written the reader cannot tell which value wins.

examples.source: You can set options when initializing Sampler, after initializing Sampler, or you can update the options after Sampler has been initialized.
examples.translation: Maaari kang magtakda ng mga opsyon kapag sinisimulan ang Sampler, pagkatapos masimulan ang Sampler, o maaari mong i-update ang mga opsyon pagkatapos masimulan ang Sampler.
examples.suggested: ... kapag ini-initialize ang Sampler, pagkatapos i-initialize ang Sampler, o maaari mong i-update ang mga opsyon pagkatapos ma-initialize ang Sampler.
examples.why: "sinisimulan/masimulan" means "started/begun", not object initialization; Filipino devs keep "i-initialize". Recognizable but imprecise for an API concept.

examples.source: Limits how long a job can run, in seconds.
examples.translation: Nilimitahan ang tagal ng pagpapatakbo ng isang trabaho, sa mga segundo.
examples.suggested: Nililimitahan ang tagal ng pagpapatakbo ng isang trabaho, sa mga segundo.
examples.why: Perfective "Nilimitahan" reads as a past event; the option description is a standing behavior, so the imperfective "Nililimitahan" is what a native technical writer would use here.

examples.source: the interface of the primitives' `run()` method / the `run()` method
examples.translation: ang interface ng `run()` na pamamaraan ng mga primitive ... / sa pamamaraang `run()`
examples.suggested: ang interface ng pamamaraang `run()` ng mga primitive ... (match the later form)
examples.why: English adjective-before-noun order is calqued in the first instance, then the natural linker form is used two paragraphs later — same construction rendered two ways within the file.

editor_note: Two sentences would actively mislead a learner. In the Description section, "sparsity" is rendered as the non-word "paguusok" ("Sinasamantala ng mga Selected Configuration Interaction (SCI) na pamamaraan ang paguusok na ito") — "usok" is smoke, so the entire rationale for SCI (that only a few configurations matter) becomes unintelligible; it should be "kakauntian"/"pagkakalat" or a kept "sparsity". Worse, the optimization-loop paragraph swaps the quantity being minimized: English "minimizing the number of configurations included" becomes "pinipigilan ang bilang ng mga kasama sa configuration" (limiting the number of members *inside a configuration*), which teaches the wrong invariant about how HI-VQE keeps the subspace compact. Two smaller agent inversions compound this: "assuming you've already saved your account" → "kung nai-save na **nito** ang iyong account" (the tool saved it, not you), and "If you want help with troubleshooting" → "Kung gusto mong **makatulong** sa pag-troubleshoot" (you offering help rather than receiving it). Minor on top: "intractable" strengthened to "imposible", the qualifiers in "very loose termination criteria" and "saving computation resources significantly" are dropped, "demonstrated benchmark calculations" → "ipinahayag" (announced), and "raise an exception" calqued as "magtataas ng exception". Register is otherwise correctly informal and domain terms (qubit, subspace, ground state, eigenvector, shots) are kept in English consistently.

examples.source: Selected configuration interaction (SCI) methods exploit this sparsity to reduce computational costs
examples.translation: Sinasamantala ng mga Selected Configuration Interaction (SCI) na pamamaraan ang paguusok na ito para mabawasan ang mga gastos sa computation
examples.suggested: Sinasamantala ng mga Selected Configuration Interaction (SCI) na pamamaraan ang sparsity na ito (na kakaunti lang ang mahalagang configuration) para mabawasan ang gastos sa computation
examples.why: "paguusok" is not a Tagalog word for sparsity — its root "usok" means smoke. The whole justification for SCI (only a small fraction of configurations matters) becomes unreadable; the learner cannot recover the concept.

examples.source: iteratively refining a subspace to optimally represent the ground state while minimizing the number of configurations included
examples.translation: paulit-ulit na pinipino ang isang subspace para optimal na marepresenta ang ground state habang pinipigilan ang bilang ng mga kasama sa configuration
examples.suggested: ...habang pinapaliit ang bilang ng mga configuration na isinasama
examples.why: Swapped quantity: the English minimizes how many configurations go into the subspace; the Tagalog says it limits the number of members inside a configuration. The learner forms a false picture of what HI-VQE keeps compact.

examples.source: If you want help with troubleshooting a specific error, please provide the Function job ID
examples.translation: Kung gusto mong makatulong sa pag-troubleshoot ng isang partikular na error, mangyaring ibigay ang Function job ID
examples.suggested: Kung gusto mong matulungan sa pag-troubleshoot ng isang partikular na error, ibigay ang Function job ID
examples.why: "makatulong" inverts the direction of help — it reads as the user volunteering to assist, not requesting support.

examples.source: assuming you've already saved your account to your local environment
examples.translation: kung nai-save na nito ang iyong account sa iyong lokal na environment
examples.suggested: kung na-save mo na ang iyong account sa iyong lokal na environment
examples.why: "nito" shifts the agent from the reader to the tool, so the prerequisite step the user must perform is no longer stated as theirs.

examples.source: calling job.result() will raise an exception
examples.translation: ang pagtawag sa `job.result()` ay magtataas ng exception
examples.suggested: magre-raise / maglalabas ng exception ang pagtawag sa `job.result()`
examples.why: "magtataas" is a literal calque of "raise" (to lift physically); no Tagalog-speaking engineer writes this — the field keeps "raise" or uses "maglabas".

editor_note: Meaning is broadly faithful — the benchmark numbers (30 shots vs 170,000, 99% confidence, `ibm_sherbrooke`), the $A$ metric definition, the "not a hard cap, larger problems have been solved" caveat, and the Sampler/Estimator workflow all survive intact, and the register stays casual (mo/iyong, no po/opo). What a native editor would change are false-friend word choices and one omission: "increased quantum runtime" (an overhead item) becomes "pinahusay na quantum runtime" ("improved"), flipping a cost into a benefit inside the overhead list; "not a hard limitation" becomes "hindi isang mahirap na limitasyon" ("not a difficult limitation"), the wrong sense of "hard"; and "increase the spread" becomes "palakihin ang kalat", where bare "kalat" reads as litter/mess rather than statistical spread ("pagkakalat"/"saklaw"). The table's "highest count bitstring" is misparsed twice as "ang pinakamataas na bilang ng bitstring" ("the highest number of bitstrings"), even though the same idea is rendered correctly later as "ang bitstring na may pinakamataas na bilang ng counts" — an in-file inconsistency. Also, the step heading "**3. Plot the top bitstrings**" (EN line 292) is dropped entirely from the walkthrough, and "gumagawa sa parehong gate at pulse na antas" should be "gumagana" (operates), not "gumagawa" (makes).

examples.source: eliminates the need for additional overhead, such as increased quantum runtime or extra physical qubits
examples.translation: Inaalis ng pipeline ng Fire Opal ang pangangailangan para sa karagdagang overhead, tulad ng pinahusay na quantum runtime o dagdag na pisikal na qubit.
examples.suggested: ...tulad ng mas mahaba/karagdagang quantum runtime o dagdag na pisikal na qubit.
examples.why: "pinahusay" means improved/enhanced, turning an overhead cost (more runtime) into a benefit; the surrounding "karagdagang overhead" barely rescues it, but the item itself now reads backwards.

examples.source: The "Number of qubits" indicated is not a hard limitation but represents rough thresholds
examples.translation: Ang "Bilang ng mga qubit" na ipinahiwatig ay hindi isang mahirap na limitasyon kundi kumakatawan sa magaspang na mga threshold
examples.suggested: ...ay hindi isang mahigpit na limitasyon kundi kumakatawan sa tantiyang mga threshold
examples.why: "mahirap" is the wrong sense of "hard" (difficult, not strict); "magaspang" is the texture sense of "rough". A learner could read it as conceding there IS a limitation, just an easy one.

examples.source: Percentage of runs where the correct answer is the highest count bitstring
examples.translation: Porsyento ng mga run kung saan ang tamang sagot ay ang pinakamataas na bilang ng bitstring
examples.suggested: Porsyento ng mga run kung saan ang tamang sagot ang bitstring na may pinakamataas na bilang
examples.why: The noun phrase is misparsed as "the highest number of bitstrings" instead of "the bitstring with the highest count", garbling the success-rate definition in both table rows; line 338 renders the same idea correctly, so the file is also internally inconsistent.

examples.source: or increase the spread, the value of A should remain consistent
examples.translation: o palakihin ang kalat, dapat manatiling consistent ang halaga ng $A$
examples.suggested: o palawakin ang pagkakalat/saklaw, dapat manatiling consistent ang halaga ng $A$
examples.why: Bare "kalat" reads as litter/mess in Tagalog; no native technical writer would use it for statistical spread.

examples.source: **3. Plot the top bitstrings**
examples.translation: (omitted — the TL jumps straight to "I-plot ang bitstring na may pinakamataas na bilang...")
examples.suggested: **3. I-plot ang mga nangungunang bitstring**
