editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim (three node colors, apply_operation_back vs _front, TransformationPass modifies / AnalysisPass only extracts info, the `distance != 1` swap-insertion logic, layer-by-layer traversal over disjoint qubit sets) matches the English, and the informal register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would change is phrasing: the "Create and transpile against custom backends" link is calqued as "mag-transpile **laban sa** mga custom na backend", where "laban sa" reads as "in opposition to" rather than "targeting"; "Finally, the pass should be registered..." becomes "**Sa wakas**, ang pass ay dapat irehistro..." (the at-last-with-relief sense; "Panghuli" is the technical connector); and "traversing/traversed the DAG layer-by-layer" is rendered as "pagtatakbo sa DAG" / "ang DAG ay tinatakbo", which reads as running rather than walking through the graph. There is also a verb split on "implement": the heading uses "Ipatupad ang isang BasicMapper pass" while the body says "isang `BasicMapper` pass ay **isinasagawa**" and "Ang pangunahing functionality ay **isinasagawa** sa `run(dag)` method" — the same verb also carries "executed" two paragraphs later ("maaaring isagawa nang nakapag-iisa"), blurring implement vs. execute without making either unidentifiable. Prose is also uniformly "Ang X ay [verb]" passive where Tagalog technical writing would front the verb ("Idinaragdag ang isang operasyon sa dulo ng DAGCircuit gamit ang..."), which is what gives the page its slightly MT-ish cadence.

examples.source: Learn how to [Create and transpile against custom backends]
examples.translation: Alamin kung paano [Lumikha at mag-transpile laban sa mga custom na backend]
examples.suggested: Alamin kung paano [Gumawa at mag-transpile para sa mga custom na backend]
examples.why: "laban sa" is the adversarial "against" (versus/opposing). English "transpile against a backend" means targeting it. A Tagalog reader parses the current wording as transpiling in opposition to the backend.

examples.source: Finally, the pass should be registered within the `qiskit.transpiler.passes` module.
examples.translation: Sa wakas, ang pass ay dapat irehistro sa loob ng `qiskit.transpiler.passes` module.
examples.suggested: Panghuli, dapat irehistro ang pass sa loob ng `qiskit.transpiler.passes` module.
examples.why: "Sa wakas" carries the "at long last / finally, after all that trouble" sense; the enumerative connector in technical prose is "Panghuli". Also fronting the verb removes the stiff "ang X ay dapat" passive.

examples.source: a `BasicMapper` pass is implemented … The main functionality is then implemented in the `run(dag)` method … can thus be executed independently
examples.translation: isang `BasicMapper` pass ay isinasagawa … Ang pangunahing functionality ay isinasagawa sa `run(dag)` method … maaaring isagawa nang nakapag-iisa
examples.suggested: isang `BasicMapper` pass ang ipinapatupad … Ipinapatupad ang pangunahing functionality sa `run(dag)` method … (keep "maaaring isagawa" for "executed")
examples.why: The heading already uses "Ipatupad" for implement, but the body switches to "isinasagawa", which the same file uses for "executed". Recognizable in context, but it makes "implement" and "execute" collapse into one verb.

examples.source: It does so by traversing the DAG layer-by-layer … the DAG is traversed layer-by-layer
examples.translation: Ginagawa ito sa pamamagitan ng pagtatakbo sa DAG layer-by-layer … ang DAG ay tinatakbo layer-by-layer
examples.suggested: Ginagawa ito sa pamamagitan ng pagdaan sa DAG nang paisa-isang layer … dinadaanan ang DAG nang paisa-isang layer
examples.why: "pagtatakbo/tinatakbo" reads as running (or running code) rather than walking a graph; "pagdaan sa" / "dinadaanan" is the natural rendering of traversal for a Tagalog-speaking engineer.

editor_note: No misleading content: every quantitative and conditional claim survives intact — six observables ("anim na two-qubit na Pauli operator"), the entanglement signature (independent X/Z = 0, XX/ZZ correlations = 1), the ⟨Z_1Z_0⟩ = 1 vs ⟨I_1⊗Z_0⟩⟨Z_1⊗I_0⟩ = 0 contrast, "mahigit 100 qubit at mahigit 1000 gate", and the decay of ⟨Z_0Z_i⟩ with increasing i "kahit na sa isang ideal na simulation ... dapat na 1". Register is consistently informal (mo/ka, no po/opo) and core terms are stable in English where the field keeps them (qubit, circuit, observable, expectation value, backend, Estimator/Sampler, transpile-adjacent ISA). What a native editor would change: the simulator callout renders "you can instead use the following code" as "maaari mo ring gamitin" ("you can ALSO use"), losing the instead/alternative framing; the "Next steps" list header "Try one of these tutorials:" is dropped entirely so the three tutorial links float without their framing; "measurement(s)" is rendered as the noun "sukat" (= size) in the Operator Notation admonition and in Step 4 ("`dict` ng mga sukat") where "pagsukat"/"sukatan" is the natural technical noun; and "nagpapainstansya ng tunay na device" is a stiff coinage for "instantiates" that no Tagalog engineer would write.

examples.source: To save time, you can instead use the following code to run this small workload on the `fake_provider`…
examples.translation: Para makatipid ng oras, maaari mo ring gamitin ang sumusunod na code para patakbuhin ang maliit na workload na ito sa `fake_provider`…
examples.suggested: Para makatipid ng oras, maaari mong gamitin sa halip ang sumusunod na code…
examples.why: 'ring' means 'also', turning an either/or alternative into an additive suggestion; the reader may think the fake_provider run is done in addition to the hardware run rather than in place of it. Meaning is recoverable from context, so minor.

examples.source:
-   Try one of these tutorials:
  - [Ground-state energy estimation of the Heisenberg chain with VQE]…
examples.translation: - [Ground-state energy estimation ng Heisenberg chain gamit ang VQE]…
examples.suggested:
- Subukan ang isa sa mga tutorial na ito:
    - [Ground-state energy estimation ng Heisenberg chain gamit ang VQE]…
examples.why: The list header introducing the three tutorial links is dropped, so the tutorials sit at the same level as the install/credentials guides and lose their grouping — flattened structure in a Recommendations block whose whole job is to steer the learner.

examples.source: the measurement of ⟨Z_1 Z_0⟩ … a `dict` of measurements in the form of bitstrings
examples.translation: ang sukat ng ⟨Z_1 Z_0⟩ … `dict` ng mga sukat sa anyo ng mga bitstring
examples.suggested: ang pagsukat ng ⟨Z_1 Z_0⟩ … `dict` ng mga measurement/sukatan sa anyo ng mga bitstring
examples.why: 'sukat' as a bare noun reads as 'size/dimension'; the act or outcome of measuring is 'pagsukat' or 'sukatan'. Recognizable in context but not the term a Tagalog technical writer would pick, and the file elsewhere correctly uses the verb form 'susukatín'.

examples.source: The following code instantiates a real device to submit a job to and transforms the circuit and observables…
examples.translation: Ang sumusunod na code ay nagpapainstansya ng tunay na device para makapag-submit ng job…
examples.suggested: Ang sumusunod na code ay gumagawa ng instance ng tunay na device na pagsa-submit-an ng job…
examples.why: 'nagpapainstansya' is an invented Tagalog affixation of 'instantiate' that no native engineer writes; the idiomatic pattern is 'gumagawa ng instance ng'. Grammatical but audibly machine-made.

examples.source: as the distance between qubits increases, the signal decays
examples.translation: habang lumalayo ang distansya sa pagitan ng mga qubit, ang signal ay bumababa
examples.suggested: habang lumalaki ang distansya sa pagitan ng mga qubit, humihina ang signal
examples.why: Distance 'lumalayo' (moves away) is a category slip — it is the qubits that get farther apart, the distance 'lumalaki'. 'Bumababa' for a decaying signal is also weaker than 'humihina'/'nanghihina'. Style-level only; the physics still reads correctly.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim tracks the English, including the tricky last 40% (the `ExecutionSpan.mask` paragraph keeps "True para sa lahat ng mga shot na naisakatuparan sa panahon ng window nito" and the `(2,3)` → `(2,3,4)` shape example intact, and the closing Admonition preserves both halves of the overlap caveat — "hindi kinakailangan na ang mga limitasyon ng window ng oras ay kasing-tight na posible"). What a native technical editor would change is wording, not meaning: OOP "instances" is rendered as "mga halimbawa" ("examples") in the `ExecutionSpans` paragraph, which is the wrong sense of the word — "mga instance" is the conventional rendering. Several calqued constructions survive: the trailing "…upang sukatin ang circuit gamit" (mirrors the stranded English "to measure the circuit with"), "i-bind ang circuit laban sa $\theta_k$" ("against" taken adversarially), the axis description "tumatakbo sa mga ordenadong shot" for "runs over", and "pandaigdigang impormasyon" for scope-sense "global" (geographic sense; "pangkalahatang" is meant). Minor term wobble too: "measurements/measurement values" is mostly "sukat" (which reads as "size") while the bullet uses "pagsukat"; and the opening paragraph stutters "Pagkatapos, pagkatapos makumpleto ang trabaho". Register is correctly casual throughout — no po/opo.

examples.source: This object is a list-like container containing instances of subclasses of `ExecutionSpan`, such as `SliceSpan`.
examples.translation: Ang bagay na ito ay isang container na katulad ng listahan na naglalaman ng mga halimbawa ng mga subclass ng `ExecutionSpan`, tulad ng `SliceSpan`.
examples.suggested: ... na naglalaman ng mga instance ng mga subclass ng `ExecutionSpan`, tulad ng `SliceSpan`.
examples.why: OOP "instances" became "mga halimbawa" (= examples). Recognizable in context but the wrong sense of the word; a reader sees "examples of subclasses" rather than actual objects.

examples.source: (Optionally) a number of shots to measure the circuit with
examples.translation: (Opsyonal) isang bilang ng mga shot upang sukatin ang circuit gamit
examples.suggested: (Opsyonal) isang bilang ng shots na gagamitin sa pagsukat ng circuit
examples.why: The dangling "gamit" at the end is a direct calque of the stranded English preposition "with"; Tagalog cannot leave it hanging and the phrase reads as unfinished.

examples.source: View global information about the collection of execution spans:
examples.translation: Tingnan ang pandaigdigang impormasyon tungkol sa koleksyon ng mga execution span:
examples.suggested: Tingnan ang pangkalahatang impormasyon tungkol sa koleksyon ng mga execution span:
examples.why: "Pandaigdigan" means global in the worldwide/geographic sense; the intended meaning is aggregate/overall scope, which is "pangkalahatan".

examples.source: Then, after the job has completed, the results are returned in a format that is dependent on ...
examples.translation: Pagkatapos, pagkatapos makumpleto ang trabaho, ang mga resulta ay ibinabalik sa isang format na nakasalalay sa ...
examples.suggested: Kapag natapos na ang trabaho, ibinabalik ang mga resulta sa isang format na nakadepende sa ...
examples.why: "Pagkatapos, pagkatapos" repeats the same word twice in a row — an artifact of translating "Then, after" literally; no native technical writer would leave the stutter.

examples.source: the input must contain measurements / measurement instructions / actual measurement values
examples.translation: dapat maglaman ng mga sukat / mga tagubilin sa pagsukat / aktwal na mga halaga ng sukat
examples.suggested: Use "pagsukat" consistently: "dapat maglaman ng mga pagsukat", "mga halaga ng pagsukat"
examples.why: Bare "sukat" primarily reads as "size/dimension" in Tagalog, and the file alternates it with the correct "pagsukat" within a few lines — an inconsistency worth unifying.

editor_note: The migration guidance is substantively faithful — removals, the `if_test` replacement path, the `Target`-indexing example, and the September 2024 / March 2025 support dates all survive intact, and the register stays casual throughout with no po/opo. The clearest defect is in the `getattr(operation, "condition", None)` paragraph, where "cause `Instruction` instances to behave as they did in Qiskit v1.x" became "magpapaliwanag ng `Instruction` instances" ("will EXPLAIN the instances") — the wrong verb for "behave"; "kikilos ang mga `Instruction` instance na gaya ng sa Qiskit v1.x" is what is meant. Two smaller meaning slips: "preferentially represented by ... `IfElseOp`" loses "preferentially" (TL just says "kinakatawan na"), and "more expressive" is twice rendered "mas maliwanag" (= clearer/brighter) rather than more expressive/mapaghayag. Remaining nits are calques a native technical writer would rewrite — "magtataas ng `UserWarning`" (literal "raise"; native is "maglalabas ng"/"may ila-labas na") and "maliit na ginagamit na package" for "little-used package" (should be "bihirang gamitin").

examples.source: which will typically cause `Instruction` instances to behave as they did in Qiskit v1.x and earlier
examples.translation: na kadalasan ay magpapaliwanag ng `Instruction` instances na parang nasa Qiskit v1.x at mas lumang bersyon
examples.suggested: na kadalasan ay magiging dahilan para kumilos ang mga `Instruction` instance gaya ng ginawa nila sa Qiskit v1.x at mas luma
examples.why: 'magpapaliwanag' means 'will explain'; the source claim is about runtime BEHAVIOR under the legacy attribute, so the compatibility guarantee is garbled.

examples.source: Classical conditions in Qiskit have been preferentially represented by the instruction `IfElseOp` since before Qiskit v1.0.
examples.translation: Ang mga classical condition sa Qiskit ay kinakatawan na ng instruction na `IfElseOp` bago pa ang Qiskit v1.0.
examples.suggested: ... ay mas pinipiling katawanin ng instruction na `IfElseOp` mula pa bago ang Qiskit v1.0.
examples.why: 'preferentially' is dropped, turning a statement about the preferred representation into a flat statement that this WAS the representation.

examples.source: the more expressive classical computation subsystem / a more expressive communication of these constraints
examples.translation: mas maliwanag na [classical computation subsystem] / mas maliwanag na komunikasyon ng mga constraint
examples.suggested: mas mapaghayag / mas malawak ang kayang ipahayag
examples.why: 'maliwanag' means clear/bright, not expressive; the point is expressive POWER (can encode more complex conditions), not clarity.

examples.source: the Qiskit team no longer had resources to maintain the little-used package
examples.translation: ang Qiskit team ay wala nang mapagkukunan para mapanatili ang maliit na ginagamit na package
examples.suggested: wala nang rekurso ang Qiskit team para mapanatili ang bihirang gamiting package
examples.why: 'maliit na ginagamit' is a word-for-word calque of 'little-used' that no Tagalog technical writer would produce.

examples.source: from v2.0 a `UserWarning` will be raised
examples.translation: mula sa v2.0 ay magtataas ng `UserWarning`
examples.suggested: mula sa v2.0 ay maglalabas na ito ng `UserWarning`
examples.why: 'magtataas' is the physical sense of 'raise'; for exceptions/warnings Tagalog technical prose uses 'maglalabas ng' or keeps the verb in English.

editor_note: No misleading content: every claim in the source survives intact — the `exclusive=true`/`exclusive=false` contrast, the "walang ibang scheduling ng mga user na sangkot sa labas ng Slurm" caveat, "maliban kung awtomatikong natukoy mula sa CRN", and the "walang shared na cluster-wide na quantum access" parenthetical are all correctly rendered, and infrastructure terms (job, node, backend, endpoint, kredensyal, execution lane) are kept consistently. What a native editor would fix is grammar, concentrated in the last 40%: line 148's "maaaring mayroon ng kasinami na mga job tulad ng mga execution lane" is garbled — the comparative should be "kasindami ng mga execution lane", and "ang job ay itinalaga ng isang lane" uses the wrong marker (assigned *by* a lane instead of "itinatalaga sa isang lane"). Line 141 has "ay pamamahalaan lamang" where the aspect should be "pinamamahalaan lamang", line 147 calques "at the same time as" into "sa parehong oras bilang isang non-exclusive na job" (natural: "kasabay ng"), and line 40 has a typo "magtaturo" for "magtuturo". Register is correctly casual throughout with no po/opo; "user" is split between "gumagamit" (headings) and "user" (body), which is defensible but uneven.

examples.source: there can be as many jobs as there are execution lanes, all running at the same time, and the job is assigned one lane
examples.translation: maaaring mayroon ng kasinami na mga job tulad ng mga execution lane, lahat ay tumatakbo sa parehong oras, at ang job ay itinalaga ng isang lane
examples.suggested: maaaring magkaroon ng mga job na kasindami ng mga execution lane, lahat ay sabay na tumatakbo, at ang bawat job ay itinatalaga sa isang lane
examples.why: 'kasinami na ... tulad ng' is not a valid Tagalog comparative (should be 'kasindami ng'), and 'itinalaga ng isang lane' marks the lane as the agent doing the assigning rather than the thing assigned.

examples.source: cannot run at the same time as a non-exclusive job
examples.translation: hindi maaaring tumakbo sa parehong oras bilang isang non-exclusive na job
examples.suggested: hindi maaaring tumakbo nang kasabay ng isang non-exclusive na job
examples.why: 'bilang' calques the English 'as' in its role/identity sense, so it reads as 'running in the capacity of a non-exclusive job' instead of the comparative 'at the same time as'.

examples.source: The capacity and priority of the QPU usage is solely managed through Slurm
examples.translation: Ang kapasidad at priyoridad ng paggamit ng QPU ay pamamahalaan lamang sa pamamagitan ng Slurm
examples.suggested: Ang kapasidad at priyoridad ng paggamit ng QPU ay pinamamahalaan lamang sa pamamagitan ng Slurm
examples.why: 'pamamahalaan' is the wrong verb form here; the statement of fact needs the imperfective 'pinamamahalaan'.

examples.source: lists the quantum resource names (comma-separated if several are provided)
examples.translation: inililista ... ang mga pangalan ng quantum resource (pinaghihiwalay ng kuwit kung ilang ang ibinibigay)
examples.suggested: (pinaghihiwalay ng kuwit kung marami ang ibinibigay)
examples.why: 'kung ilang ang ibinibigay' is ungrammatical as a conditional; 'marami' or 'higit sa isa' carries the English 'if several'.

examples.source: `SBATCH` parameters will point to one or more QPU resources
examples.translation: Ang mga parameter ng `SBATCH` ay magtaturo sa isa o higit pang mga QPU resource
examples.suggested: Ang mga parameter ng `SBATCH` ay magtuturo sa isa o higit pang mga QPU resource
examples.why: Simple typo in the verb ('magtaturo' for 'magtuturo').

editor_note: No misleading content: the retirement date (15 Mayo 2024), the 50-qubit ceiling, the "walang built-in na error suppression o mitigation" caveat, the Open Plan sessions warning, and the 500-qubit Clifford example all match the source, and register is consistently casual with no po/opo. The defects are wording, not meaning. "high-performance supercomputers" is rendered as "mataas na kalidad na mga supercomputer" (= high *quality*), which loses the performance sense and clashes with the untranslated "high-performance simulation" left in the same file's table row. "builds skills" is calqued twice as "nagtatayo ng ... kasanayan" (literally *erects/constructs* skills — a native writer would use "nagpapaunlad/nagpapatibay ng kasanayan"), matched by "mag-drive ng inobasyon" for "drive innovation"; "with verifiable results" comes out as "may mga nave-verify na resulta", an awkward coinage where "napapatunayan/mave-verify na mga resulta" reads naturally. There is also a small grammar slip in "Ino-retire ang mga cloud simulator sa ilang dahilan" (should be "dahil sa ilang dahilan" / "para sa ilang dahilan").

examples.source: their usefulness maxes out at around 50 qubits, even with access to high-performance supercomputers
examples.translation: hanggang sa humigit-kumulang 50 qubit lang ang kanilang pagiging kapaki-pakinabang, kahit may access sa mataas na kalidad na mga supercomputer
examples.suggested: ... kahit may access sa mga high-performance na supercomputer
examples.why: 'high-performance' becomes 'mataas na kalidad' (high quality), a different property; the same English term is left untranslated in the comparison table ('high-performance simulation'), so the file is also internally inconsistent.

examples.source: Using quantum hardware builds unique skills / Direct interaction with quantum hardware builds skills
examples.translation: Nagtatayo ng natatanging kasanayan ang paggamit ng quantum hardware / ... ay nagtatayo ng mga kasanayan
examples.suggested: Nagpapaunlad ng natatanging kasanayan ... / ... ay nagpapatibay ng mga kasanayan
examples.why: 'nagtatayo' is the literal 'builds/erects' used for structures; applied to skills it is a calque no Tagalog technical writer would use. Note the very next bullet already uses the idiomatic 'nagpapaunlad', so the file is inconsistent with itself.

examples.source: Because Clifford circuits can be simulated efficiently with verifiable results
examples.translation: Dahil ang mga Clifford circuit ay maaaring i-simulate nang episyente na may mga nave-verify na resulta
examples.suggested: Dahil episyenteng ma-si-simulate ang mga Clifford circuit at napapatunayan ang mga resulta nito
examples.why: 'nave-verify' is a malformed aspect form and the stacked 'nang episyente na may' is stiff MT rhythm; meaning survives but the sentence reads translated, not written.

examples.source: The cloud simulators are being retired for several reasons:
examples.translation: Ino-retire ang mga cloud simulator sa ilang dahilan:
examples.suggested: Ino-retire ang mga cloud simulator dahil sa ilang dahilan:
examples.why: 'sa ilang dahilan' drops the causal marker; as written it reads closer to 'in a few reasons' than 'for several reasons'. Purely a grammar slip, not a meaning change.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner: the negation in "hindi makakapagsumite ng mga session job" is intact, "kahit isang circuit at isang observable" correctly renders "at least one", the batch/session/backend mapping keeps "ayon sa pagkakasunod" (respectively), and PUB/ISA/expectation value/observable/transpiler are kept in English consistently throughout. The residual issues are editorial polish only. (1) In step 2, machine "instructions" is rendered "mga tagubilin" ("directions/guidelines"), which is the wrong sense for ISA instructions even though the parenthetical *instruction set architecture (ISA)* rescues it — a native technical writer would keep "instructions" or use "mga instruction/utos". (2) "may ilang built-in na mga teknik" doubles the plural marker (ilang + mga), a stiffness an editor would trim to "ilang built-in na teknik". (3) The intro clause "para sa isa o higit pang mga observable na may kaugnayan sa mga state na inihanda ng mga quantum circuit" attaches "with respect to states" to the observables rather than to the expectation-value computation — meaning survives, but the phrasing is a calque of the English "with respect to".

examples.source: The circuit and observable need to be transformed to only use instructions supported by the QPU (referred to as *instruction set architecture (ISA)* circuits).
examples.translation: Ang circuit at observable ay kailangang i-transform para gumamit lamang ng mga tagubilin na sinusuportahan ng QPU (tinatawag na *instruction set architecture (ISA)* circuit).
examples.suggested: ... para gumamit lamang ng mga instruction na sinusuportahan ng QPU ...
examples.why: "tagubilin" is the everyday word for guidance/directions, not hardware instructions; with ISA sitting right beside it the learner still gets it, so this is an imperfect-but-recognizable term, not a false concept.

examples.source: This primitive has several built-in error mitigation and suppression techniques, including dynamical decoupling, Pauli-twirling, gate-folding ZNE, PEA, and PEC.
examples.translation: Ang primitive na ito ay may ilang built-in na mga teknik ng [error mitigation at suppression], kabilang ang dynamical decoupling, ...
examples.suggested: May ilang built-in na teknik ng [error mitigation at suppression] ang primitive na ito, kabilang ang ...
examples.why: "ilang ... mga" stacks two plural markers, and the fronted "Ang primitive na ito ay" is the stiff ay-inversion; a native technical writer would use the verb-initial order.

examples.source: The Estimator primitive computes the expectation values for one or more observables with respect to states prepared by quantum circuits.
examples.translation: Kinakalkula ng Estimator primitive ang mga expectation value para sa isa o higit pang mga observable na may kaugnayan sa mga state na inihanda ng mga quantum circuit.
examples.suggested: ... ang mga expectation value ng isa o higit pang observable kaugnay ng mga state na inihanda ng mga quantum circuit.
examples.why: "na may kaugnayan sa" is a literal rendering of "with respect to" and syntactically hangs off "observable" instead of the computation; meaning is preserved but it reads as translationese.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic inversion, swapped quantity, softened claim, dropped caveat, or hallucinated sentence, including in the last 40% (Optimization/Scheduling), and domain terms (qubit, gate, circuit, layout, routing, depth, native/basis gate, stochastic) are kept in English consistently, which is the right convention here. What a native technical editor would still fix: a genuine typo in the VF2Layout bullet, "Kung mahiit sa isang layout ang mahanap" (intended "mahigit sa isang layout" = more than one layout) — "mahiit" is not a word and momentarily garbles the condition; an untranslated English adverb inside Tagalog syntax, "isang maganda ngunit hindi necessarily optimal na SWAP mapping"; and a repeated calque "mag-account/pag-account para sa idle time" (three times in the Scheduling section) where a Tagalog writer would say "isaalang-alang ang idle time". Smaller stiffness: "ng Backend na padadalhang circuit" for "the backend a circuit will be sent to" (should be "kung saan ipapadala ang circuit"), "Sa wakas" used for "Finally" in a step sequence (should be "Panghuli"), "idinisenyo lamang para magtrabaho sa single- at two-qubit gate" (algorithms "gumagana sa", not "nagtatrabaho"), and "hanggang sa maging magkatabing muli sila" which adds an "again" the English does not have. Register is correctly casual — no po/opo anywhere.

examples.source: If more than one layout is found, a scoring heuristic is run to select the mapping with the lowest average error.
examples.translation: Kung mahiit sa isang layout ang mahanap, nagpapatakbo ng scoring heuristic para piliin ang mapping na may pinakamababang average error.
examples.suggested: Kung mahigit sa isang layout ang mahanap, isang scoring heuristic ang pinapatakbo para piliin ang mapping na may pinakamababang average error.
examples.why: "mahiit" is not a Tagalog word — a typo for "mahigit" that briefly garbles the condition; the verb is also left dangling agentless ("nagpapatakbo ng..." with no subject).

examples.source: ...to compute a good, but not necessarily optimal, SWAP mapping.
examples.translation: ...para makalkula ang isang maganda ngunit hindi necessarily optimal na SWAP mapping.
examples.suggested: ...para makakuha ng magandang SWAP mapping, kahit hindi naman ito palaging pinakamainam.
examples.why: "necessarily" is left in raw English inside Tagalog syntax — pure code-switch translationese, not a kept domain term.

examples.source: These passes focus on accounting for all the idle time in a circuit. / to account for idle time on each qubit / to account for any timing constraints
examples.translation: nakatuon sa pag-account para sa lahat ng idle time / para mag-account para sa idle time sa bawat qubit / para mag-account para sa anumang timing constraint
examples.suggested: nakatuon sa pagsasaalang-alang ng lahat ng idle time / para isaalang-alang ang idle time sa bawat qubit / para tugunan ang anumang timing constraint
examples.why: "mag-account para sa" is a direct calque of "account for" repeated three times in the Scheduling section; a Tagalog technical writer would use isaalang-alang/tugunan.

examples.source: The next stage involves the layout or connectivity of the backend a circuit will be sent to.
examples.translation: Ang susunod na yugto ay kinabibilangan ng layout o connectivity ng Backend na padadalhang circuit.
examples.suggested: ...ng layout o connectivity ng Backend kung saan ipapadala ang circuit.
examples.why: "Backend na padadalhang circuit" collapses the English relative clause into an ungrammatical modifier — the reader has to reconstruct which noun is being sent.

examples.source: Finally, a padding pass such as PadDelay or PadDynamicalDecoupling can be executed.
examples.translation: Sa wakas, maaaring isagawa ang isang padding pass tulad ng `PadDelay` o `PadDynamicalDecoupling`.
examples.suggested: Panghuli, maaaring isagawa ang isang padding pass tulad ng `PadDelay` o `PadDynamicalDecoupling`.
examples.why: "Sa wakas" carries a sense of relief ("at long last"); the English "Finally" here is just the last step in an ordered sequence, which is "Panghuli".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats: the min_qpy_version bullet keeps "mas mababa kaysa sa tinukoy dito", RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4 correctly gives "apat na thread", QISKIT_FORCE_THREADS keeps the "para maiwasan ang potensyal na pag-overload ng limitadong CPU resources" rationale, and QISKIT_SABRE_ALL_THREADS keeps the non-reproducibility tradeoff and the ">20 CPU/core" figure. What a native technical editor would still change is verb morphology/voice in three spots: "magtatanggihan" (min_qpy_version) is a malformed form of "tatanggihan"; "ang multithreaded na code ay palaging magsasagawa sa maraming thread" uses the actor-focus verb where the code is what runs, so it should be "tatakbo/isasagawa sa maraming thread"; and "Mapabubuti nito ang kalidad ng mga resulta" asserts the improvement where the English hedges with "can improve" ("Maaari nitong mapabuti" would match). None of these would lead a learner to a false belief.

examples.source: QPY loading will reject files with a QPY version lower than the one defined here.
examples.translation: Ang pag-load ng QPY ay magtatanggihan ng mga file na may QPY version na mas mababa kaysa sa tinukoy dito.
examples.suggested: Tatanggihan ng pag-load ng QPY ang mga file na may QPY version na mas mababa kaysa sa tinukoy dito.
examples.why: "magtatanggihan" is not a well-formed verb here (the reciprocal/-han shape); a native writer would use the goal-focus "tatanggihan". Meaning still comes through, so this is a fluency slip only.

examples.source: Specifies that multithreaded code should always execute in multiple threads.
examples.translation: Tinutukoy na ang multithreaded na code ay palaging magsasagawa sa maraming thread.
examples.suggested: Tinutukoy na ang multithreaded na code ay dapat palaging tumakbo (isagawa) sa maraming thread.
examples.why: "magsasagawa" is actor-focus ("will carry out"), but the code is what is executed, not the executor of something else; also the deontic "should" is flattened to a plain future.

examples.source: This can improve the quality of the results, especially for systems with greater than 20 CPUs/cores
examples.translation: Mapabubuti nito ang kalidad ng mga resulta, lalo na para sa mga sistema na may higit sa 20 CPU/core
examples.suggested: Maaari nitong mapabuti ang kalidad ng mga resulta, lalo na para sa mga sistema na may higit sa 20 CPU/core
examples.why: The English hedges ("can improve"); the Tagalog future "Mapabubuti nito" reads closer to a promise. Borderline given the potentive ma- prefix, so minor rather than misleading, but the explicit "maaaring" would match the source's caution.

editor_note: The arithmetic sense of "odd" is rendered twice as "kakaiba" (= strange/unusual), which destroys the parity concept the page teaches: in the For-loop section "Because it performs an odd number of X gates" becomes "Dahil nagsasagawa ito ng kakaibang bilang ng mga X gate" ("a strange number of X gates"), and in the Classical-expressions walkthrough "the parity of all preceding bits is odd" becomes "ang parity ng lahat ng naunang bit ay kakaiba" ("the parity ... is strange"). Tagalog for odd-numbered is "gansal" (or "hindi pares"); as written, the learner cannot recover the actual rule (parity = 1) that drives the X correction, so the code comment "Add X if parity is 1" no longer matches the prose. Secondary, non-blocking slips: "significantly more efficient at runtime" drops the intensifier ("mas mahusay ang iyong code sa runtime"); "take advantage of" becomes "mapagsamantalahan", which in Tagalog carries an exploitative connotation a technical writer would avoid ("masulit"/"magamit nang husto"); and aspect errors give the wrong tense — "Ipinaliwanag ng natitirang bahagi ng gabay" (past, for present "explains"), "pagkatapos ay susukat ito" and "Sa wakas, susukat ng ikatlong qubit" (future, actorless, for imperative/present "measure").

examples.source: Because it performs an odd number of X gates, the overall effect is to flip the qubit from the 0 state to the 1 state.
examples.translation: Dahil nagsasagawa ito ng kakaibang bilang ng mga X gate, ang pangkalahatang epekto ay baligtarin ang qubit mula sa estado 0 patungo sa estado 1.
examples.suggested: Dahil nagsasagawa ito ng gansal (odd) na bilang ng mga X gate, ...
examples.why: "kakaiba" means strange/unusual, not odd-numbered. The parity argument — the entire reason 5 X gates net to a flip — is lost, and the learner is told something the English never says.

examples.source: You apply $X$ to every unmeasured site for which the parity of all preceding bits is odd.
examples.translation: Mag-aaplay ka ng $X$ sa bawat hindi nasukat na site kung saan ang parity ng lahat ng naunang bit ay kakaiba.
examples.suggested: ... kung saan gansal (odd) ang parity ng lahat ng naunang bit — ibig sabihin, katumbas ng 1.
examples.why: "parity ... ay kakaiba" is semantically empty; the actual condition (parity = 1) becomes unrecoverable, contradicting the accompanying code comment "Add X if parity is 1" and teaching a false version of the GHZ correction rule.

examples.source: Operations are automatically parallelized, making your code significantly more efficient at runtime.
examples.translation: Ang mga operasyon ay awtomatikong ina-parallelize, na ginagawang mas mahusay ang iyong code sa runtime.
examples.suggested: ... na ginagawang mas mahusay nang malaki ang iyong code sa runtime.
examples.why: "significantly" is dropped, softening the claim about the benefit of using `store`.

examples.source: While these are early days of understanding how best to take advantage of dynamic circuits
examples.translation: Bagama't maaga pa lamang ang pag-unawa kung paano pinakamabuti na mapagsamantalahan ang dynamic circuits
examples.suggested: Bagama't maaga pa lamang ang pag-unawa kung paano pinakamahusay na magagamit ang dynamic circuits
examples.why: "mapagsamantalahan" carries the exploitative sense of pagsasamantala in Tagalog; no native technical writer would use it for "take advantage of" a technique.

examples.source: The remainder of this guide explains each of these constructs and how to use them.
examples.translation: Ipinaliwanag ng natitirang bahagi ng gabay na ito ang bawat isa sa mga construct na ito at kung paano ito gamitin.
examples.suggested: Ipinapaliwanag ng natitirang bahagi ng gabay na ito ...
examples.why: Perfective aspect reads as "has already explained", inverting the forward-pointing signpost the English gives the reader; the same aspect problem recurs in "susukat ito" (line ~195) and "Sa wakas, susukat ng ikatlong qubit" (line ~163), which is also actorless where the English is an imperative.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the tricky spots all survive intact: the negation in "kung ang `precision` ay hindi tinukoy ng anumang PUB o sa run keyword argument (o kung lahat sila ay `None`)", the "lahat ng apat na lugar" precedence example, the twirling-failure caveat ("mabibigo ang trabaho kung ang `twirling` ay pinagana at ang produkto ... ay mas maliit kaysa sa mga shots na kailangan"), and the inverse-scaling note ("mas mababa ang precision, mas maraming QPU time"). No drift, no hallucination, informal register holds (mo/mong, no po/opo). What a native technical editor would still change is surface: the concessive "while" is calqued as temporal "Habang ... ay karaniwan sa lahat ng implementasyon" (should be "Bagama't pareho ang interface ..."), the adverb "Specifically" is left untranslated at the head of the precedence list, "job" is rendered two ways in the same file ("trabaho" in the max_execution_time and twirling notes vs. bare "job" in the Feature-compatibility and Next-steps sections), and there are several stiff literalisms — "sa gastos ng mas mahabang oras ng pagpoproseso", "Gaano karaming resilience ang itatayo", "sa pagitan ng isang sukat", and the heading "Mga opsyong Available".

examples.source: While the interface of the primitives' `run()` method is common across all implementations, their options are not.
examples.translation: Habang ang interface ng pamamaraan ng `run()` ng mga primitive ay karaniwan sa lahat ng implementasyon, ang kanilang mga opsyon ay hindi.
examples.suggested: Bagama't pareho ang `run()` na pamamaraan ng mga primitive sa lahat ng implementasyon, hindi pareho ang kanilang mga opsyon.
examples.why: "Habang" is the temporal "while" and calques the English concessive; "karaniwan" reads as "ordinary/usual" rather than "shared/the same across". Meaning still recoverable, but it is textbook translationese.

examples.source: Specifically, for any Estimator PUB:
examples.translation: Specifically, para sa anumang Estimator PUB:
examples.suggested: Partikular, para sa anumang Estimator PUB:
examples.why: An ordinary English discourse adverb left untranslated at the head of the five-step precedence list — not a domain term that the field keeps in English.

examples.source: job
examples.translation: "mabibigo ang trabaho" / "gaano katagal ang maaaring tumakbo ang isang trabaho" vs. "sa iisang job" / "para sa iyong job"
examples.suggested: Pick one — keep "job" throughout, since the runtime concept is a named Qiskit Runtime job.
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: the same runtime concept is rendered as generic "trabaho" (work/employment) in two places and kept as "job" in two others; "trabaho" also loses the technical sense.

examples.source: How much resilience to build against errors. Higher levels generate more accurate results at the expense of longer processing times.
examples.translation: Gaano karaming resilience ang itatayo laban sa mga error. Ang mas mataas na antas ay nagbibigay ng mas tumpak na mga resulta sa gastos ng mas mahabang oras ng pagpoproseso.
examples.suggested: Kung gaano karaming resilience ang bubuuin laban sa mga error. Ang mas mataas na antas ay nagbibigay ng mas tumpak na resulta kapalit ng mas mahabang oras ng pagpoproseso.
examples.why: "itatayo" is the verb for erecting a structure, and "sa gastos ng" is a word-for-word calque of "at the expense of"; a native writer uses "kapalit ng".

examples.source: The delay between a measurement and the subsequent quantum circuit.
examples.translation: Ang pagkaantala sa pagitan ng isang sukat at ng kasunod na quantum circuit.
examples.suggested: Ang pagkaantala sa pagitan ng isang pagsukat at ng kasunod na quantum circuit.
examples.why: "sukat" means a size/dimension; the act of measuring is "pagsukat". The file elsewhere keeps "measurement" in English (measurement twirling, measurement noise), so this lone native rendering is also the odd one out.

examples.source: ## Available options
examples.translation: ## Mga opsyong Available
examples.suggested: ## Mga available na opsyon
examples.why: English adjective order calqued onto Tagalog with a stray capital; the natural form places the borrowed adjective before the noun with "na".

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination anywhere — every claim (computational basis = single-qubit Pauli-Z basis, measure_all adding new classical bits in a ClassicalRegister by default, measure_active covering only non-idle qubits) matches the English, and the informal register holds with no po/opo. What a native editor would change: (1) "method" is split within the file between "paraan" (headings, "gamitin ang paraan ng `measure_all`") and "pamamaraan" ("ang pamamaraang ito ay nagdadagdag…") — same sentence, two renderings; (2) "sukat" carries both "measurement" (used ~6x) and "size" in "may sukat na katumbas ng bilang ng mga non-idle na qubit", where "laki" would avoid the collision; (3) the last bullet's caveat "(Available only when using Qiskit Runtime.)" and the link text "Mid-circuit measurements" are left wholly in English while the rest of the list was localized; (4) "para iimbak ang mga sukat na ito" is an awkward infinitive — "para maimbak" reads naturally. None of these would teach a learner anything false.

examples.source: By default, this method adds new classical bits… / This method creates a new `ClassicalRegister`…
examples.translation: gamitin ang paraan ng [`measure_all`]. Sa default, ang pamamaraang ito ay nagdadagdag… / Ang pamamaraang ito ay lumilikha…
examples.suggested: Pick one: use "paraan" throughout ("Ang paraang ito ay nagdadagdag…") to match the headings "Paraan ng `QuantumCircuit.measure_all`".
examples.why: "method" is rendered as both "paraan" and "pamamaraan" inside the same sentence and across sections; harmless but an editor would unify it.

examples.source: creates a new `ClassicalRegister` with a size equal to the number of non-idle qubits being measured
examples.translation: lumilikha ng bagong `ClassicalRegister` na may sukat na katumbas ng bilang ng mga non-idle na qubit na sinusukat
examples.suggested: …na may laki na katumbas ng bilang ng mga qubit na hindi idle na sinusukat
examples.why: The file has used "sukat" for "measurement" everywhere else, so "may sukat na katumbas" momentarily reads as "with a measurement equal to"; "laki" cleanly means size.

examples.source: - [Mid-circuit measurements](/guides/execute-dynamic-circuits#midcircuit) (Available only when using Qiskit Runtime.)
examples.translation: - [Mid-circuit measurements](/guides/execute-dynamic-circuits#midcircuit) (Available only when using Qiskit Runtime.)
examples.suggested: - [Mga mid-circuit na sukat](…) (Available lang kapag gumagamit ng Qiskit Runtime.)
examples.why: The availability caveat is a real constraint and is the only prose in the recommendations list left untranslated, while the sibling bullets were localized to "Paraan ng…" / "Klase ng…".

examples.source: adds new classical bits in a `ClassicalRegister` to store these measurements
examples.translation: nagdadagdag ng mga bagong classical bit sa isang `ClassicalRegister` para iimbak ang mga sukat na ito
examples.suggested: …para maimbak ang mga sukat na ito
examples.why: "para iimbak" mixes the contemplated aspect after "para"; a native technical writer would write "para maimbak" (or "para itago").

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every compatibility bullet, default value, range ([1, 10800] / 3 oras), and the "value set after initialization wins" rule match the English exactly, and the informal register holds throughout with no po/opo. The defects are terminology and translationese. "measurement" in `execution.rep_delay` is rendered "isang sukat" (= a size/dimension) where the act of measuring is meant — it should be "pagsukat" or simply kept as "measurement", which is what the same file does everywhere else ("measurement twirling", "terminal measurement"), so the term is also split within the file. Separately, several sentences are calqued English syntax rather than something a Tagalog technical writer would produce: "sa panahon ng o pagkatapos ng pag-initialize" for "during or after", "kapag nagtatayo gamit ang Executor primitive" (nagtatayo = erecting a structure) for "when building with", and "nagdodokumento ng mga opsyon" for "documents options". One aspect slip: "kapag ginamit mo ang `run()`" uses completed aspect for a habitual "when you use".

examples.source: The delay between a measurement and the subsequent quantum circuit.
examples.translation: Ang pagkaantala sa pagitan ng isang sukat at ng kasunod na quantum circuit.
examples.suggested: Ang pagkaantala sa pagitan ng isang measurement at ng kasunod na quantum circuit.
examples.why: "sukat" means size/dimension, not the quantum measurement operation; the rest of the file keeps "measurement" in English ("measurement twirling", "terminal measurement"), so this is both a wrong-register word and a within-file split of the same term.

examples.source: You can see the available options and update option values during or after primitive initialization.
examples.translation: ...i-update ang mga halaga ng opsyon sa panahon ng o pagkatapos ng pag-initialize ng primitive.
examples.suggested: ...i-update ang mga halaga ng opsyon habang ini-initialize ang primitive o pagkatapos nito.
examples.why: "sa panahon ng o pagkatapos ng" is a word-for-word calque of "during or after"; the stacked prepositions before a single noun phrase is not a construction a native technical writer would use.

examples.source: Those options are then applied when you use run() to perform the calculation.
examples.translation: Ang mga opsyon na iyon ay inilalapat pagkatapos kapag ginamit mo ang `run()` para magsagawa ng kalkulasyon.
examples.suggested: Inilalapat ang mga opsyong iyon kapag ginagamit mo ang `run()` para isagawa ang kalkulasyon.
examples.why: "inilalapat pagkatapos kapag" stacks two time markers awkwardly for a single "then", and "ginamit" is completed aspect where the English is habitual ("when you use").

examples.source: Specify options when building with the Executor primitive.
examples.translation: Tukuyin ang mga opsyon kapag nagtatayo gamit ang Executor primitive.
examples.suggested: Tukuyin ang mga opsyon kapag bumubuo gamit ang Executor primitive.
examples.why: "nagtatayo" is the physical sense of building (erecting a structure); "bumubuo"/"gumagawa" is the term used for constructing software.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every prose paragraph tracks the English, including the error-mitigation passage (quantum pre-processing overhead na may kaugnayan sa pagsasanay ng modelo / classical post-processing overhead) and the negated caveat in Next steps ("ang mga user ng Open Plan ay hindi makakapagsumite ng mga session job"). Terminology is consistent and correct throughout — expectation value, observable, circuit, primitive, PUB, transpile ("na-transpile na sa bagong string"), backend all kept in the field's English convention, register stays informal (iyong/mo, no po/opo). Two stiff calques a native technical editor would rewrite: "Makita ang mga detalye kung paano i-initialize..." (lines 41 and 282) is a word-for-word rendering of "Find details on how to..." — "Makita" is not usable as an imperative here; Tagalog wants "Tingnan"/"Hanapin ang mga detalye". Likewise the section heading "Magtrabaho gamit ang mga Runtime option" literally calques "Work with Runtime options" where a Tagalog docs writer would head it "Paggamit ng mga Runtime option". Neither misleads the learner.

examples.source: Find details on how to initialize your account, view available backends, and invalidate tokens in this topic.
examples.translation: Makita ang mga detalye kung paano i-initialize ang iyong account, tingnan ang mga available na Backend, at i-invalidate ang mga token sa [topic] na ito.
examples.suggested: Tingnan ang mga detalye kung paano i-initialize ang iyong account, ... sa [topic] na ito.
examples.why: 'Makita' is the ability/accidental form (maka-) and does not work as an instruction; it is a literal swap for English 'Find'. A native technical writer would use 'Tingnan' or 'Hanapin'. Meaning survives, so this is only a fluency slip — and it repeats verbatim in the Parameterized circuits section, so the fix should be applied in both places.

examples.source: ## 5. Work with Runtime options
examples.translation: ## 5. Magtrabaho gamit ang mga Runtime option
examples.suggested: ## 5. Paggamit ng mga Runtime option
examples.why: 'Magtrabaho' literally means 'to do labor/work a job' and reads oddly as a docs section head; English 'work with' here means 'use/configure'. Tagalog documentation convention nominalizes section heads ('Paggamit ng...'). Purely stylistic — no learner would be misled.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the negation in the OVHcloud admonition ("Hindi available ang mga OVHcloud AI notebook sa ilang rehiyon, tulad ng United States"), the manual-install caveat, and every numbered step map faithfully onto the English. What a native technical editor would change is grammar/voice: twice the file uses an actor-topic subject with an object-focus verb — "Ang mga gumagamit ng OVHcloud Public Cloud at OVHcloud Startup ay maaaring gamitin ang kanilang OVHcloud quantum notebooks" and "Ang mga gumagamit ng Qiskit ay maaaring gamitin ang mga preconfigured na Python environment ng qBraid" — which should be "ay maaaring gumamit ng"; as written it reads as raw calqued English syntax. Separately, the Qiskit domain term "job" is rendered as "mga trabaho" ("mag-submit ng mga trabaho sa IBM QPUs"), which reads as employment rather than a submitted quantum job — recognizable from context but not the conventional rendering (Filipino practice keeps "job"). Minor quantity softening too: "Several providers offer…" becomes "Maraming provider ang nag-aalok…" ("many"). Register is correctly casual throughout (mo/iyong, no po/opo).

examples.source: OVHcloud Public Cloud and OVHcloud Startup users can use their OVHcloud quantum notebooks… / Qiskit users can use qBraid's preconfigured Python environments…
examples.translation: Ang mga gumagamit ng OVHcloud Public Cloud at OVHcloud Startup ay maaaring gamitin ang kanilang OVHcloud quantum notebooks… / Ang mga gumagamit ng Qiskit ay maaaring gamitin ang mga preconfigured na Python environment ng qBraid…
examples.suggested: Maaaring gumamit ang mga user ng OVHcloud Public Cloud at OVHcloud Startup ng kanilang OVHcloud quantum notebooks… / Maaaring gumamit ang mga Qiskit user ng mga preconfigured na Python environment ng qBraid…
examples.why: Actor-as-topic paired with the object-focus verb 'gamitin' is a voice mismatch — a direct calque of English SVO. A Tagalog technical writer would use the actor-focus 'gumamit ng' (or recast the whole clause object-focus).

examples.source: …access Qiskit and submit jobs to IBM QPUs with their IBM Quantum or IBM Cloud account.
examples.translation: …para ma-access ang Qiskit at mag-submit ng mga trabaho sa IBM QPUs gamit ang kanilang IBM Quantum o IBM Cloud account.
examples.suggested: …at mag-submit ng mga job sa IBM QPUs…
examples.why: 'Job' here is the Qiskit domain object (a submitted execution on a QPU). 'Trabaho' is the everyday word for work/employment; Filipino technical usage keeps 'job'. Recognizable from context, but it over-translates a term the field keeps in English.

examples.source: Several providers offer online Jupyter environments with Qiskit preinstalled…
examples.translation: Maraming provider ang nag-aalok ng online na Jupyter environment na may naka-preinstall na Qiskit…
examples.suggested: May ilang provider na nag-aalok ng online na Jupyter environment na may naka-preinstall na Qiskit…
examples.why: 'Several' becomes 'maraming' ('many'), mildly strengthening the claim; the page then names only two recommended providers, so 'ilang' matches both the source and what follows.

editor_note: Content is substantively faithful — every numeric guideline survives intact (20,000–200,000 shots for <16 MOs, 200,000 for 16–18, 200,000–2,000,000 for >18; 600/1500/6000/16000 samples per batch for methanol/methylamine/water/ethanol), and the tricky heavy-hex passage ("may koneksyon lamang sa bawat ikaapat na qubit") is correct. The one real drift is a discourse connector: "In turn, this reduces the number of required S-CORE steps" became "Sa kabila nito, binabawasan nito…" ("in spite of this"), turning a consequence into a concession and stacking two contrastive markers in a row with the following "Gayunpaman"; the underlying claim still reads correctly, so it misframes rather than falsifies. The rest is translationese: the repeated calqued "ay pagkatapos + verb" pattern ("Ang LUCJ circuit ay pagkatapos na-transpile", "Ang mga bitstrings ay pagkatapos ginagamit"), a focus error in "Ang pagtawag para sa job result ay hinaharangan ang natitirang bahagi ng program", and "naka-imbak sa loob sa PySCF FCIDUMP format". Register is correctly casual throughout (no po/opo); one small term inconsistency — "two-qubit gates" is localized as "dalawang-qubit gates" in the LUCJ options section but "two-qubit depth" is left in English later.

examples.source: In turn, this reduces the number of required S-CORE steps, where only two or three iterations of SQD are needed if the number of samples per batch is large enough.
examples.translation: Sa kabila nito, binabawasan nito ang bilang ng mga kinakailangang S-CORE steps, kung saan dalawa o tatlong iteration lamang ng SQD ang kailangan kung ang bilang ng samples per batch ay sapat na malaki.
examples.suggested: Dahil dito, nababawasan ang bilang ng kinakailangang S-CORE steps, kung saan dalawa o tatlong iteration lamang ng SQD ang kailangan kung sapat na malaki ang bilang ng samples per batch.
examples.why: 'Sa kabila nito' means 'in spite of this' — a concessive. The English 'In turn' is consequential: the reduction in S-CORE steps follows FROM using more samples per batch. Combined with the 'Gayunpaman' that opens the next sentence, the paragraph's argument (benefit -> consequence -> but cost) reads as two contrasts back to back and the causal chain the passage is teaching is obscured.

examples.source: The LUCJ circuit is then transpiled into an ISA circuit for the target hardware. A Sampler primitive is then instantiated with a default set of error mitigation options to manage the execution.
examples.translation: Ang LUCJ circuit ay pagkatapos na-transpile sa isang ISA circuit para sa target hardware. Isang Sampler primitive ang pagkatapos na-instantiate na may default na set ng error mitigation options upang pamahalaan ang execution.
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos, ini-transpile ang LUCJ circuit tungo sa isang ISA circuit para sa target hardware. Susunod, ini-instantiate ang isang Sampler primitive na may default na set ng error mitigation options upang pamahalaan ang execution.
examples.why: 'ay pagkatapos + verb' is a word-for-word transplant of English 'is then …'; Tagalog does not slot 'pagkatapos' between the ay-marker and the verb, and the completed-aspect 'na-transpile' clashes with the habitual description. The same calque recurs in step 3 ('Ang mga bitstrings ay pagkatapos ginagamit bilang input').

examples.source: Calling for the job result blocks the rest of the program until a result is available.
examples.translation: Ang pagtawag para sa job result ay hinaharangan ang natitirang bahagi ng program hanggang sa may available na resulta.
examples.suggested: Hinaharangan ng pagtawag sa job result ang natitirang bahagi ng program hanggang may available na resulta.
examples.why: Focus mismatch: 'hinaharangan' is object-focus, so its actor must be marked with 'ng', not fronted as the ay-topic. As written the sentence has two competing 'ang' phrases and reads as broken Tagalog to a native technical reader.

examples.source: the input section also generates the gas-phase HF data, which is stored internally in PySCF FCIDUMP format
examples.translation: ang input section ay gumagawa rin ng gas-phase HF data, na naka-imbak sa loob sa PySCF FCIDUMP format
examples.suggested: gumagawa rin ang input section ng gas-phase HF data, na iniimbak nang internal sa PySCF FCIDUMP format
examples.why: 'sa loob sa' is a literal rendering of 'internally in' and stacks two locative markers; Tagalog would use 'nang internal' or 'sa loob ng sistema'. Meaning survives, but the phrasing is unmistakably machine-shaped.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the three plugin kinds, the "ipalit sa isa sa 6 na yugto" substitution claim, the `coupling_map` "ginagamit lamang kapag hindi tinukoy ang `target`" condition, the `None`-return caveat, and "hindi hihigit sa 3 na Qubit" (at most 3) all match the English, and no hallucinated claims appear; register stays informal (walang po/opo). What a native editor would still change: "expose" is rendered two ways — "i-expose ang class / i-expose natin ang plugin" in most places but "naglalantad ng maraming opsyon" in the unitary-synthesis options paragraph, where "naglalantad" (to bare/uncover) reads wrong for an API sense. The first-person plural is inconsistent inside single sentences ("i-expose natin ang plugin ... sa metadata ng aming Python package"), mixing inclusive natin/tayo with exclusive aming three times. Two smaller slips: "sa kaso na ang synthesis ay ginagawa sa physical circuit" is a literal calque of "in case", and the reserved-names paragraph adds "built-in" ("ilang built-in na plugins") where the source just says "a number of plugins".

examples.source: To accommodate unitary synthesis plugins that expose multiple options,
examples.translation: Para ma-accommodate ang mga unitary synthesis plugin na naglalantad ng maraming opsyon,
examples.suggested: Para ma-accommodate ang mga unitary synthesis plugin na nag-e-expose ng maraming opsyon,
examples.why: The file consistently uses "i-expose" for the API sense of expose (lines 47, 108, 277, 384); "naglalantad" means to bare/uncover physically and is the odd one out — a within-file inconsistency for the same term.

examples.source: Now, we expose the plugin by adding an entry point in our Python package metadata.
examples.translation: Ngayon, i-expose natin ang plugin sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng entry point sa metadata ng aming Python package.
examples.suggested: Ngayon, i-expose natin ang plugin sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng entry point sa metadata ng ating Python package.
examples.why: Inclusive "natin" and exclusive "aming" collide in one sentence (and again in "ang class na aming tinukoy" right after "ipinapalagay natin"); a native technical writer keeps one voice — "ating" — across the walkthrough.

examples.source: in case the synthesis is done on the physical circuit.
examples.translation: sa kaso na ang synthesis ay ginagawa sa physical circuit.
examples.suggested: kung ang synthesis ay isinasagawa sa physical circuit.
examples.why: "Sa kaso na" is a word-for-word calque of "in case" that Tagalog technical prose does not use; "kung" carries the same conditional sense naturally.

examples.source: The Qiskit SDK itself includes a number of plugins, whose names are also reserved.
examples.translation: Kasama sa Qiskit SDK ang ilang built-in na plugins, at ang kanilang mga pangalan ay nakalaan din.
examples.suggested: Kasama sa Qiskit SDK mismo ang ilang plugins, at ang kanilang mga pangalan ay nakalaan din.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the directional-ECR note, the "walang garantiya na mahahanap ang mas magandang circuit" caveat, the `ecr`-vs-`cx` default-per-QPU sentence, and the closing `VF2PostLayout` paragraph, and none invert, soften, or invent anything; terminology (coupling map, basis gates, virtual/physical qubit, transpile → i-transpile) is correct and consistent, and the informal register holds with no po/opo. The defects are grammar/fluency only, concentrated in the Coupling map paragraph: "palagi naming mababago ng transpiler ang direksyon ng gate" carries a stray first-person "naming" that has no counterpart in "the transpiler can always flip a gate's direction", and "ang mga two-qubit gate ay isang direksyon lang maaaring tumakbo" is a scrambled calque of English word order (a native writer would write "maaari lang tumakbo sa isang direksyon"). Elsewhere "mahahalagang piraso ng impormasyon" is a word-for-word calque of "essential pieces of information" where plain "mahahalagang impormasyon" is the natural Tagalog. None of these would mislead a learner about how the transpiler behaves.

examples.source: However, the transpiler can always flip a gate's direction by adding additional single-qubit gates.
examples.translation: Gayunpaman, palagi naming mababago ng transpiler ang direksyon ng gate sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng mga karagdagang single-qubit gate.
examples.suggested: Gayunpaman, palaging mababago ng transpiler ang direksyon ng gate sa pamamagitan ng pagdaragdag ng mga karagdagang single-qubit gate.
examples.why: The stray possessive pronoun "naming" (our/we) has no source counterpart and is ungrammatical next to the agent marker "ng transpiler"; it reads as an uncorrected MT artifact.

examples.source: Sometimes this graph is directional, meaning that the two-qubit gates can only go in one direction.
examples.translation: Minsan ang graph na ito ay may direksyon, ibig sabihin ang mga two-qubit gate ay isang direksyon lang maaaring tumakbo.
examples.suggested: Minsan may direksyon ang graph na ito, ibig sabihin sa isang direksyon lang maaaring gamitin ang mga two-qubit gate.
examples.why: Calqued English constituent order leaves the locative phrase stranded without "sa", and "tumakbo" (to run) is an odd verb for a gate's orientation; a native technical writer would recast the clause.

examples.source: the coupling map and supported instruction set are the essential pieces of information to pass to the transpiler
examples.translation: ang coupling map at sinusuportahang instruction set ang mahahalagang piraso ng impormasyon na ipapasa sa transpiler
examples.suggested: ang coupling map at sinusuportahang instruction set ang mahalagang impormasyong ipinapasa sa transpiler
examples.why: "piraso ng impormasyon" is a literal rendering of "pieces of information"; Tagalog treats impormasyon as a mass noun and the counter word is not used.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim tracks the English, including the three plugin kinds, the "6 na yugto" list, the counterfactual about `qiskit-toqm`/`toqm`, the "sinusubukan nang sunud-sunod hanggang sa magtagumpay ang isa sa kanila" fallback rule, and the two identical `init`/`translation`/`optimization` paragraphs. What a native editor would change: "extended (transpilation) functionality" is rendered "pinahabang functionality" throughout (3x) — "pinahaba" means lengthened/prolonged, not extended-in-scope; "pinalawak na" or "karagdagang" is the idiomatic choice. The relative clause in "ang pangalan ng yugto na gusto mong ilista ang mga plugin" drops the possessive link of "the stage WHOSE plugins you want to list" and reads as a broken clause. Core terms are otherwise correct and consistent (yugto for stage, transpile/backend/plugin/pass manager kept in English), and register stays casual with no po/opo.

examples.source: provide extended transpilation functionality
examples.translation: nagbibigay ng pinahabang transpilation functionality
examples.suggested: nagbibigay ng pinalawak (o karagdagang) na transpilation functionality
examples.why: "Pinahaba" means made longer in length or duration; "extended" here means broader in scope. Recognizable but a literal mis-pick, used consistently 3 times.

examples.source: passing the name of the stage whose plugins you want to list
examples.translation: na ipinapasa ang pangalan ng yugto na gusto mong ilista ang mga plugin
examples.suggested: at ipasa ang pangalan ng yugto na ang mga plugin ay gusto mong ilista
examples.why: The possessive "whose" relation is lost, leaving a dangling relative clause; the participial "na ipinapasa" is also calqued English syntax where an imperative "at ipasa" is what a Tagalog technical writer would use.

examples.source: create an HLSConfig to store the names of the plugins to use
examples.translation: gumawa ng HLSConfig para iimbak ang mga pangalan ng mga plugin na gagamitin
examples.suggested: gumawa ng HLSConfig para itago/i-imbak ang mga pangalan ng mga plugin na gagamitin
examples.why: After "para" the verb should be in infinitive form; "iimbak" reads as a half-formed aspect and is stiff — a minor grammatical wobble, not a meaning change.

editor_note: The Maximum executions section contains a hallucinated parenthetical: the Tagalog adds "(ang mga Estimator job ay maaaring hatiin sa mas maliliit na sub-job, kaya hindi naaangkop ang limitasyong ito)" — an assertion that the 10-million cap does not apply to Estimator jobs because they can be split into sub-jobs. Nothing of the kind appears in the English, which says only "At most, 10 million executions are allowed for Sampler jobs due to output size"; the translation also drops the actual stated reason ("due to output size") and substitutes the invented one. A learner would come away believing Estimator jobs are exempt from a documented service limit. Secondarily, the intro softens/rewrites the hedge: English "to decrease the likelihood that your job fails after you've waited for it to go through the queue" becomes "para hindi mo na kailangang maghintay sa queue at mabigo pa ang job," which reads as an assurance that this won't happen rather than a reduction in likelihood. Otherwise the prose is natural and the terminology (job, circuit, qubit, gate, shots, i-transpile, transpile→"i-transpile", talahanayan for table) is correct and consistent, and the informal register holds throughout.

examples.source: At most, **10 million** executions are allowed for Sampler jobs due to output size.
examples.translation: Pinapayagan ang hanggang **10 milyong** executions para sa mga Sampler job (ang mga Estimator job ay maaaring hatiin sa mas maliliit na sub-job, kaya hindi naaangkop ang limitasyong ito).
examples.suggested: Pinapayagan ang hanggang **10 milyong** executions para sa mga Sampler job dahil sa laki ng output.
examples.why: Hallucination plus a dropped reason: the parenthetical about Estimator jobs being split into sub-jobs and being exempt from the limit exists nowhere in the source, and the source's actual justification ("due to output size") is deleted. This teaches a false exemption from a real service limit.

examples.source: it is first validated to try to ensure that the job can run on the QPU, to decrease the likelihood that your job fails after you've waited for it to go through the queue
examples.translation: Sinisikap ng serbisyong ito na matiyak na makakatakbo ang job sa QPU para hindi mo na kailangang maghintay sa queue at mabigo pa ang job.
examples.suggested: ...para mabawasan ang tsansang mabigo ang job pagkatapos mong maghintay sa queue.
examples.why: "decrease the likelihood" is a hedge; "para hindi mo na kailangang maghintay ... at mabigo pa" reads as a guarantee that the wait-then-fail outcome is eliminated, strengthening the claim the English deliberately qualifies.

examples.source: are no longer relevant or enforced
examples.translation: ay hindi na relevant o ipinapatupad
examples.suggested: ay hindi na angkop o ipinapatupad
examples.why: Bare English adjective "relevant" sits awkwardly beside the otherwise fully Tagalog clause; a native technical writer would use "angkop"/"may saysay" here since "relevant" is not a domain term the field keeps in English. Minor polish only.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful throughout — the exam mechanics survive intact ("20 tanong", "hindi bababa sa 16 para makapasa", "kung hindi ka makakuha ng passing score sa dalawang pagkakataon, pansamantalang mala-lock ang pagsusulit"), no drift, no dropped caveat, no hallucination, and register stays casual ("Binabati kita", "i-click ang pindutan sa ibaba"). The problems are all in the Credly/privacy paragraph at the end: "Ito ay pamamahalain" uses a malformed verb (the correct form is "pamamahalaan"), and "mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM" renders "privacy practices" as "kasanayan" (skills/habits) where a native technical writer would use "mga kagawian/patakaran sa privacy". One earlier calque, "Mangyaring ilaan ang isang sandali", mirrors English "take a moment" word-for-word instead of the idiomatic "Maglaan ka ng sandali". None of these would mislead a learner about the course or the exam.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ito ay pamamahalain sa paraang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kagawian sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.why: "pamamahalain" is a non-standard verb form (the -an focus of pamahalaan is "pamamahalaan"), and the "Ito ay ..." frame is a stiff English-passive calque a native technical writer would avoid.

examples.source: ...consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: ...naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.suggested: ...naaayon sa mga kagawian/patakaran sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.why: "kasanayan" means skill or proficiency; "practices" in a privacy-policy sense is "kagawian" or "patakaran". Recognizable but the wrong sense of the word.

examples.source: Please take a moment to help us improve our course...
examples.translation: Mangyaring ilaan ang isang sandali para tulungan kaming mapabuti ang aming kurso...
examples.suggested: Maglaan ka ng sandali para tulungan kaming mapabuti ang kursong ito...
examples.why: "ilaan ang isang sandali" is a word-for-word calque of "take a moment"; the numeral "isang" is redundant in Tagalog and the imperative reads more stiffly than the surrounding casual register.

editor_note: No claim here would teach a learner anything false — domain terms (quantum mechanics, superposition, simulator, Open Plan, linear algebra, matrix) are kept in English consistently and the informal register holds throughout, with no po/opo. But the last bullet loses the source's actual point: "most notebooks can simply be run as written" becomes "maaaring patakbuhin nang basta-basta lang", where "basta-basta" means "haphazardly/carelessly" and the load-bearing "as written" (i.e. no code editing needed) is gone — it should read "gaya ng pagkakasulat" or "nang hindi na binabago". Two calques also read as MT rather than native technical writing: "answer keys" → "susi sa sagot" (a Filipino instructor says "sagutang gabay"/"answer key"), and "fit into an undergraduate course" → "makasalang sa", an odd collocation where "umangkop sa" is the natural verb. Finally, "much less than the free time allotted" drops the intensifier and becomes a bare "mas mabilis kaysa sa libreng oras", weakening the reassurance the paragraph is making.

examples.source: Some Python familiarity, though most notebooks can simply be run as written
examples.translation: Kaunting karanasan sa Python, kahit na karamihan sa mga notebook ay maaaring patakbuhin nang basta-basta lang
examples.suggested: Kaunting karanasan sa Python, bagaman karamihan sa mga notebook ay puwedeng patakbuhin gaya ng pagkakasulat (walang kailangang baguhin)
examples.why: 'basta-basta lang' means 'haphazardly/carelessly', not 'as written'. The pedagogical reassurance — that the code needs no modification — disappears and is replaced by a sloppiness connotation.

examples.source: versions of these notebooks with answer keys and guidance on placement in common curricula
examples.translation: mga bersyon ng mga notebook na ito na may susi sa sagot at gabay sa paglalagay sa karaniwang mga kurikulum
examples.suggested: mga bersyon ng mga notebook na ito na may sagutang gabay (answer key) at rekomendasyon kung saan ito ilalagay sa karaniwang kurikulum
examples.why: 'susi sa sagot' is a word-for-word calque of 'answer key'; 'gabay sa paglalagay' is stiff nominalized English syntax no Filipino instructor would write.

examples.source: is designed to fit into an undergraduate quantum mechanics course
examples.translation: ay dinisenyo upang makasalang sa isang undergraduate na kurso sa quantum mechanics
examples.suggested: ay dinisenyo upang umangkop sa isang undergraduate na kurso sa quantum mechanics
examples.why: 'makasalang' (to be put on the fire / set into a process) is the wrong collocation for 'fit into a course'; 'umangkop sa' is the idiomatic verb.

examples.source: All activities can be completed in much less than the free time allotted as part of the Open Plan
examples.translation: Lahat ng aktibidad ay maaaring tapusin nang mas mabilis kaysa sa libreng oras na inilaan bilang bahagi ng Open Plan
examples.suggested: Lahat ng aktibidad ay matatapos nang mas maikli pa nang malayo kaysa sa libreng oras na inilaan bilang bahagi ng Open Plan
examples.why: 'much less' is flattened to a plain comparative, softening the source's explicit assurance that there is ample margin in the free quota.

editor_note: No misleading content: every table row preserves its direction and mechanism ("Bawasan ang circuit width at depth sa pamamagitan ng pagputol ng mga gate at wire", "para sa pagbawas ng PEC sampling overhead"), the Binder / "sarili mong Jupyter server" disjunction is intact, and register is consistently informal with no po/opo. Two word-choice slips a native technical editor would fix: "specialized quantum computing algorithms" is rendered "mga espesyal na quantum computing algorithm", where "espesyal" means merely "special" rather than specialized/dalubhasa, flattening the claim that these addons target narrow domains; and "ground state estimation" is rendered "pagtataya ng ground state", where "pagtataya" reads primarily as forecast/prediction rather than numerical estimation ("pagtatantiya"/"estimasyon" is the standard technical rendering). Both remain recognizable to a learner, so neither misleads. Nothing else in the prose needs changing.

examples.source: official extension packages that provide specialized quantum computing algorithms and techniques
examples.translation: mga opisyal na extension package na nagbibigay ng mga espesyal na quantum computing algorithm at teknik
examples.suggested: mga opisyal na extension package na nagbibigay ng mga espesyalisadong quantum computing algorithm at teknik
examples.why: "espesyal" carries the sense of "special/nice", not "specialized"; the English point is that each addon covers a narrow, dedicated area, which "espesyalisado" preserves and "espesyal" softens.

examples.source: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization for ground state estimation
examples.translation: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization para sa pagtataya ng ground state
examples.suggested: Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization para sa pagtatantiya ng ground state
examples.why: "pagtataya" reads as forecasting/predicting (also "betting"); SQD numerically estimates the ground state, for which "pagtatantiya"/"estimasyon" is the conventional Tagalog technical term.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveat, no hallucination; the 4-hour estimate, the "no technical prerequisite" clause, the Quantum Business Foundations prerequisite recommendation and the IBM Quantum Learning contact line all match the source, and register stays informal (no po/opo). Two things a native technical editor would still change: the heading "Nilalayon na audience" is a word-for-word calque of "Intended audience" that no Tagalog tech writer would write (idiomatic: "Para kanino ang kursong ito" or "Target na audience"), and "inirerekumenda naming mauna munang kunin ng mga mag-aaral ang kurso sa [Quantum Business Foundations]" stacks the redundant "mauna" + "muna" and reads stiffly. There is also a cosmetic spelling split of the same root within the file: the heading uses "Inirekomendang background" while the body twice uses "Inirerekumenda". None of this would mislead a learner.

examples.source: ### Intended audience
examples.translation: ### Nilalayon na audience
examples.suggested: ### Para kanino ang kursong ito (o: Target na audience)
examples.why: Direct calque of the English noun phrase; "nilalayon na audience" is not how a Tagalog technical writer heads this section, though it is understandable.

examples.source: we recommend that learners first take the [Quantum Business Foundations] course
examples.translation: inirerekumenda naming mauna munang kunin ng mga mag-aaral ang kurso sa [Quantum Business Foundations]
examples.suggested: inirerekomenda naming kunin muna ng mga mag-aaral ang [Quantum Business Foundations] na kurso
examples.why: "mauna munang" doubles the same "first" sense, and "ang kurso sa X" reads as "the course in X"; meaning is intact but the phrasing is redundant and stiff.

examples.source: Recommended background / We recommend...
examples.translation: "Inirekomendang background" (heading) vs "Inirerekumenda" (body, twice)
examples.suggested: Use one spelling of the root consistently, e.g. "Inirerekomenda" / "Inirerekomendang background"
