editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated sentences; domain terms (quantum teleportation, quantum key distribution (QKD), linear algebra, simulator, notebook) are kept in English consistently, which is the right convention here, and the register stays casual with no po/opo. Three things a native technical editor would still fix. (1) "sakaling aksidente ng mga mag-aaral na maubos ang kanilang libreng oras" is ungrammatical calquing of "in case students accidentally exhaust"; the adverb "accidentally" has been turned into a noun ("aksidente ng mga mag-aaral"), which no Tagalog writer would produce — should be "sakaling hindi sinasadyang maubos ng mga mag-aaral". (2) "answer keys" is rendered literally as "mga susi ng sagot", which reads as physical keys; the field keeps "answer key" in English or uses "susi sa pagwawasto". (3) The intensifier in "much less time than the free time allotted" is flattened to plain "mas maikling panahon" — a dropped qualifier, not misleading but it loses the English's reassurance that there is ample margin. Also minor: "kung mayroon sila ng" should be "kung mayroon silang".

examples.source: Simulator options are also built-in in case students accidentally exhaust their free quantum computing time.
examples.translation: Ang mga opsyon ng simulator ay nakasama rin sakaling aksidente ng mga mag-aaral na maubos ang kanilang libreng oras sa quantum computing.
examples.suggested: May kasama ring mga opsyon para sa simulator sakaling hindi sinasadyang maubos ng mga mag-aaral ang kanilang libreng oras sa quantum computing.
examples.why: "accidentally" (adverb) is nominalized into "aksidente ng mga mag-aaral", producing an ungrammatical clause that reads as machine output; "nakasama" is also a weak rendering of "built-in".

examples.source: versions of these notebooks with answer keys
examples.translation: mga bersyon ng mga notebook na ito na may mga susi ng sagot
examples.suggested: mga bersyon ng mga notebook na ito na may kasamang answer key
examples.why: "mga susi ng sagot" is a literal calque where "susi" reads as a physical key; Tagalog technical/education writing keeps "answer key" or uses "susi sa pagwawasto".

examples.source: All activities can be completed in much less time than the free time allotted as part of the Open Plan
examples.translation: Ang lahat ng gawain ay maaaring makumpleto sa mas maikling panahon kaysa sa libreng oras na inilaan bilang bahagi ng Open Plan
examples.suggested: ...sa mas maikli nang husto na panahon kaysa sa libreng oras na inilaan bilang bahagi ng Open Plan
examples.why: The intensifier "much" is dropped, softening the English's assurance of a comfortable margin to a bare "less time"; the claim is still true but the pedagogical reassurance is flattened.

editor_note: Index page with no body prose; the only translatable strings are rendered naturally and correctly — title "Learning"→"Pag-aaral", "Courses"→"Mga Kurso", "Modules"→"Mga Modyul" (correct Filipino orthography, not the calqued "Mga Module") — and the 15 course link labels plus URLs are left verbatim as proper titles, which matches the file's link-list structure exactly.

Meaning is fully faithful — nothing here would mislead a learner: the exam mechanics survive intact ("20 tanong… hindi bababa sa 16 para makapasa", "Kung hindi ka makakakuha ng passing score sa dalawang pagtatangka, pansamantalang mala-lock ang pagsusulit"), no dropped caveat, no inverted condition, no hallucinated sentence, and the Credly/privacy notice is complete. Register is correctly casual (kita/iyong, no po/opo). What a native technical editor would change is the English-passive "ay" calque, which recurs across most of the second half — "Ang iyong feedback ay gagamitin", "Ang iyong badge ay awtomatikong ipapadala", "Ang iyong personal na impormasyon ay ginagamit", "Ito ay pamamahalaan sa paraang naaayon", "Ang IBM Privacy Statement ay maaaring tingnan dito" — where idiomatic Tagalog fronts the verb; the effect is stiff, MT-signature prose rather than something a Filipino technical writer would produce. Secondary nit: "karanasan ng gumagamit" for "user experience" is an over-translation of a term the field keeps as "user experience"/"karanasan ng user".

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices. The IBM Privacy Statement can be viewed here.
examples.translation: Ito ay pamamahalaan sa paraang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM. Ang IBM Privacy Statement ay maaaring tingnan [dito.]
examples.suggested: Pamamahalaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM. Maaaring tingnan [dito] ang IBM Privacy Statement.
examples.why: Direct calque of the English passive with 'ay'-inversion; natural Tagalog fronts the verb. Grammatical but reads as machine output, not native technical prose.

examples.source: your badge will automatically be sent to the email you used to register with IBM Training
examples.translation: ang iyong badge ay awtomatikong ipapadala sa email na ginamit mo para mag-register sa IBM® Training
examples.suggested: awtomatikong ipapadala ang iyong badge sa email na ginamit mo sa pag-register sa IBM® Training

examples.source: Your feedback will be used to enhance our content offering and user experience.
examples.translation: Ang iyong feedback ay gagamitin para mapahusay ang aming mga nilalaman at karanasan ng gumagamit.
examples.suggested: Gagamitin ang iyong feedback para mapahusay ang aming mga nilalaman at ang karanasan ng user.
examples.why: 'gumagamit' is a literal rendering of 'user'; Filipino tech writing keeps 'user' (or 'user experience'). Meaning is unaffected — style/terminology only.

editor_note: No physics is taught wrongly — "sukat (measurements)", "projective measurements", "quantum state discrimination/tomography" and "density matrix" all survive intact, and the register stays casual (no po/opo). But four native-editor slips remain. "concepts discussed previously in the course" becomes "tinalakay kanina sa kurso", where "kanina" means "a little while ago today", not "earlier in the course" (should be "naunang tinalakay"). "one of a known collection of states" is mis-parsed as "isa sa mga kilalang koleksyon ng mga estado" — "one of the known collections" — pluralizing the collection instead of picking a state out of it; the following clause "kung aling estado ang inihanda" rescues the meaning, so it confuses rather than misleads. "John Watrous steps you through the content" becomes "tinutugunan ni John Watrous ang mga nilalaman" ("addresses"), losing the walk-you-through sense. Finally "state" is inconsistent — "mga estado" in one clause, "state na iyon" in the next sentence — and "are made available" is calqued as "ang ginagawang available".

examples.source: and we'll connect them to concepts discussed previously in the course.
examples.translation: at iuugnay natin ang mga ito sa mga konsepto na tinalakay kanina sa kurso.
examples.suggested: at iuugnay natin ang mga ito sa mga konseptong naunang tinalakay sa kurso.
examples.why: "kanina" is a same-day temporal adverb ("a while ago"), not "earlier in the course"; a native technical writer would use "naunang tinalakay" or "sa mga naunang aralin".

examples.source: where a system is prepared in one of a known collection of states
examples.translation: kung saan inihanda ang isang sistema sa isa sa mga kilalang koleksyon ng mga estado
examples.suggested: kung saan inihanda ang isang sistema sa isa sa mga estado mula sa isang kilalang koleksyon
examples.why: The Tagalog reads as "one of the known collections of states", moving the selection from a state to a collection. The next clause ("kung aling estado ang inihanda") restores the intent, so it garbles rather than teaches a false idea.

examples.source: which state was prepared … a density matrix description of that state
examples.translation: kung aling estado ang inihanda … ang density matrix na paglalarawan ng state na iyon
examples.suggested: Pick one: either "estado" throughout, or keep "state" in English throughout.
examples.why: "state" is rendered as "estado" in one sentence and left as English "state" in the very next one; the concept stays identifiable, but the split is exactly the kind of thing an editor unifies.

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson on general measurements.
examples.translation: tinutugunan ni John Watrous ang mga nilalaman ng araling ito sa pangkalahatang mga sukat
examples.suggested: gagabayan ka ni John Watrous sa mga nilalaman ng araling ito tungkol sa pangkalahatang mga sukat
examples.why: "tinutugunan" means "addresses/responds to", which drops the guided walkthrough sense of "steps you through" — the pedagogical framing of the video intro flattens.

examples.source: many independent copies of a single, unknown quantum state are made available
examples.translation: maraming independiyenteng kopya ng iisang hindi kilalang quantum state ang ginagawang available
examples.suggested: …ang ibinibigay sa atin / ang inilalaan
examples.why: "ginagawang available" is a literal calque of "are made available" with unnecessary code-switching; native technical Tagalog uses "ibinibigay" or "inilalaan".

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every clause of the source is present and faithful, including the duplicated IBM Cloud Logs paragraph (lines 16 and 20), the audit-compliance caveat ("para sumunod sa mga kinakailangan ng regulasyon sa pag-audit"), and all ten table rows. The one real defect is the table header "Triggered by" rendered as "Itinaas ng" — literally "raised/lifted by", which reads as a mis-picked sense of "trigger"; a native technical editor would write "Na-trigger ng" or "Idinulot ng". Secondary stiffness: "isang platform na serbisyo" is a calque of "a platform service" (natural Tagalog would be "isang serbisyo ng platform"), and "ma-alert sa mga kaganapan" copies English "alert on" rather than something like "makatanggap ng alerto para sa mga kaganapan". Register is consistently informal (mo/iyong, no po/opo), and backend/job/instance/UI are kept in English consistently throughout.

examples.source: | Action | Triggered by |
examples.translation: | Aksyon | Itinaas ng |
examples.suggested: | Aksyon | Na-trigger ng |
examples.why: "Itinaas" is the "raise/lift up" sense, not the event-triggering sense; as a column header over API calls it momentarily reads as "raised by" and forces the reader to infer the meaning from the row content. Recognizable, so minor, but not the term a Tagalog engineer would pick.

examples.source: IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing, a platform service,
examples.translation: IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing, isang platform na serbisyo,
examples.suggested: IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing, isang serbisyo ng platform,
examples.why: English noun-adjunct order calqued directly into Tagalog; "platform na serbisyo" is grammatical but stiff, where the genitive "serbisyo ng platform" is how a native technical writer would phrase it.

examples.source: to visualize and alert on events that are generated in your account
examples.translation: para ma-visualize at ma-alert sa mga kaganapang nabuo sa iyong account
examples.suggested: para makita at makatanggap ng mga alerto para sa mga kaganapang nabuo sa iyong account
examples.why: "ma-alert sa" transplants the English phrasal verb "alert on"; in Tagalog the ma- prefix suggests the reader is the one being alerted rather than configuring alerts on events. Meaning still recovers from context, so minor.

editor_note: The lesson's key claim is modally softened: English "In general, this will affect the state of the systems that were not measured" becomes "Sa pangkalahatan, maaari nitong maapektuhan ang estado ng mga sistemang hindi nasukat" — "may/can affect" instead of "will affect". That inserted hedge ("maaari") turns the central teaching point of the paragraph, that measuring part of a multi-system state generally does disturb the unmeasured remainder, into a mere possibility, so a learner reading only the Tagalog would come away with a weaker and wrong belief about partial measurement. Two smaller slips: "steps you through the content" is rendered as "isinasalaysay... ang nilalaman" (narrates/recounts), losing the guided walk-through sense a native technical writer would give as "gagabayan ka"; and the intensifier in "this idea *very* directly leads to" is dropped in "direktang humahantong". Terminology and register are otherwise sound and consistent (quantum state, measurement, entanglement, qubit kept in English; casual register with no po/opo).

examples.source: In general, this will affect the state of the systems that were not measured, and it is important to understand exactly how when analyzing quantum algorithms and protocols.
examples.translation: Sa pangkalahatan, maaari nitong maapektuhan ang estado ng mga sistemang hindi nasukat, at mahalaga na maunawaan nang eksakto kung paano kapag sinusuri ang mga quantum algorithm at protocol.
examples.suggested: Sa pangkalahatan, maaapektuhan nito ang estado ng mga sistemang hindi nasukat, at mahalagang maunawaan nang eksakto kung paano kapag sinusuri ang mga quantum algorithm at protocol.
examples.why: 'will affect' is a definite assertion; 'maaari nitong maapektuhan' downgrades it to 'may affect'. This is the paragraph's whole pedagogical payload — that partial measurement does disturb the unmeasured subsystems — so the hedge teaches the learner something weaker than the source.

examples.source: John Watrous steps you through the content in this lesson on multiple systems.
examples.translation: isinasalaysay ni John Watrous ang nilalaman ng araling ito tungkol sa multiple systems
examples.suggested: gagabayan ka ni John Watrous sa nilalaman ng araling ito tungkol sa multiple systems
examples.why: 'isinasalaysay' means narrates/recounts, which reads like a storyteller rather than an instructor walking the viewer through material; 'gagabayan ka' is what a Tagalog technical writer would use for 'steps you through'.

examples.source: Indeed, this idea very directly leads to a description of how quantum states, measurements, and operations work for multiple systems.
examples.translation: Sa katunayan, ang ideyang ito ay direktang humahantong sa paglalarawan kung paano gumagana ang mga quantum state, measurement, at operasyon para sa maraming sistema.
examples.suggested: Sa katunayan, ang ideyang ito ay napakadirektang humahantong sa paglalarawan kung paano gumagana ang mga quantum state, measurement, at operasyon para sa maraming sistema.
examples.why: The intensifier 'very' is dropped, flattening the author's emphasis that the compound-system view leads immediately to the full multi-system formalism. Minor on its own.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the deprecation dates/versions, the "both $R_X(\theta)$ at $R_ZZ(\theta)$ ay kailangang i-load" obligation, and the calibration definition ("isang mapa sa pagitan ng isang `ScheduleBlock` at isang gate sa isang `QuantumCircuit`") all match the English, and Taglish terminology (qubit, gate, backend, pulse-level na kontrol, flag) is correct and consistent. Two fluency-only slips remain. In the second paragraph, "Ang karaniwang proseso ay gumamit ng `RXCalibrationBuilder` … at magdagdag ng …" makes "proseso" the actor of actor-focus verbs and mixes completed (gumamit) with contemplated (magdagdag) aspect; a native technical writer would nominalize to "ang paggamit … at ang pagdaragdag …". Minor also: "pinaka-karaniwang" is normally written unhyphenated (pinakakaraniwang), and "Ang pagbabagong ito ay hinimok ng…" is a stiff passive where "Naudyukan ang pagbabagong ito ng…" reads more naturally.

examples.source: The typical process was to use the `RXCalibrationBuilder` and `RZXCalibrationBuilder` (or `RZXCalibrationBuilderNoEcho`) and add either a `RXGate` or `RZXGate` instruction to a QPU's `target`
examples.translation: Ang karaniwang proseso ay gumamit ng `RXCalibrationBuilder` at `RZXCalibrationBuilder` (o `RZXCalibrationBuilderNoEcho`) at magdagdag ng `RXGate` o `RZXGate` na instruksyon sa `target` ng isang QPU
examples.suggested: Ang karaniwang proseso ay ang paggamit ng `RXCalibrationBuilder` at `RZXCalibrationBuilder` (o `RZXCalibrationBuilderNoEcho`) at ang pagdaragdag ng `RXGate` o `RZXGate` na instruksyon sa `target` ng isang QPU
examples.why: 'Proseso' is made the actor of actor-focus verbs, and the two verbs disagree in aspect (completed 'gumamit' vs contemplated 'magdagdag'). Nominalizing (paggamit / pagdaragdag) is what a native technical writer would use after 'Ang karaniwang proseso ay'. Meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: This change was motivated by our ongoing focus on utility-scale experiments
examples.translation: Ang pagbabagong ito ay hinimok ng aming patuloy na pagtuon sa utility-scale na mga eksperimento
examples.suggested: Naudyukan ang pagbabagong ito ng aming patuloy na pagtuon sa utility-scale na mga eksperimento
examples.why: The 'Ang X ay <verb>' pattern is a calque of the English passive; fronting the verb reads more naturally in Tagalog technical prose. Also in the same paragraph, 'pinaka-karaniwang' (line 14) is conventionally written unhyphenated as 'pinakakaraniwang'.

editor_note: The file is one prose paragraph plus a link list; the list, URLs and front matter match the source exactly, register is correctly casual ("panatilihing secure ang iyong mga sistema", no po/opo), and nothing is hallucinated or inverted. One qualifier is dropped: English "keep your systems as secure as possible" becomes plain "Napakahalaga na panatilihing secure ang iyong mga sistema" — the "as ... as possible" (hangga't maaari) degree is gone, so the advice reads as a binary state rather than a best-effort maximum. Everything else ("lubos na inirerekumenda", "awtomatikong nagpapaalam kapag may mga lumang dependency") is faithful and idiomatic; no misleading content.

examples.source: It is vitally important that you keep your systems as secure as possible.
examples.translation: Napakahalaga na panatilihing secure ang iyong mga sistema.
examples.suggested: Napakahalaga na panatilihing kasing-secure ng makakaya ang iyong mga sistema. (o: ...secure hangga't maaari...)
examples.why: The degree qualifier "as secure as possible" is dropped, softening the source's best-effort framing into a flat "keep them secure". Not misleading, but an editor would restore it.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every conditional, negation and caveat survives intact — the crucial "it does *not* depend on the size of the quantum circuit" is rendered correctly as "*hindi* ito nakasalalay sa laki ng quantum circuit", and the "never go without the protection" clause is faithfully "hindi kailanman mawawalan ng proteksyon". What a native technical editor would change is wording. The conditional "as long as" is rendered inconsistently within the file: correctly as "hangga't" in the opening paragraph and in the closing threshold-theorem sentence, but as the temporal "habang" ("while") in the key threshold sentence, which reads as a time clause rather than a condition. Three other spots are stiff calques rather than how a Tagalog quantum writer would put it: "Lahat ito ay nagtatakda ng malaking hamon" (nagtatakda = stipulates/sets, not presents), "may katapusang threshold value" for "finite" (natural is "may hangganan"), and "kritikal na mahalagang katotohanan" for "critically important fact". Register is correctly casual throughout, no po/opo.

examples.source: as long as the level of noise falls below a certain *threshold value*
examples.translation: habang ang antas ng ingay ay nasa ibaba ng isang tiyak na *threshold value*
examples.suggested: hangga't ang antas ng ingay ay nasa ibaba ng isang tiyak na *threshold value*
examples.why: "habang" is temporal ("while"); the sentence states a condition, not a period of time. The same file already uses the correct conditional "hangga't" in line 9 and line 27, so this is an internal inconsistency in rendering the identical English connective.

examples.source: This all presents a major challenge.
examples.translation: Lahat ito ay nagtatakda ng malaking hamon.
examples.suggested: Malaking hamon ang lahat ng ito. / Naghaharap ito ng malaking hamon.
examples.why: "nagtatakda" means to set/stipulate/prescribe — it does not collocate with "hamon". A native technical writer would use "naghaharap ng" or simply restate it predicatively.

examples.source: falls below a certain finite threshold value
examples.translation: nasa ibaba ng isang tiyak na may katapusang threshold value
examples.suggested: nasa ibaba ng isang tiyak na may-hangganang threshold value
examples.why: "may katapusan" reads as "has an ending / is not everlasting" (temporal) rather than the mathematical "finite". "May hangganan" is the conventional Tagalog rendering for a finite bound. Meaning is still recoverable, so this is minor, not misleading.

examples.source: the quantum gates, measurements, and state initializations ... will themselves be imperfect
examples.translation: ang mga quantum gate, measurement, at state initialization ... ay magiging may depekto rin
examples.suggested: ... ay hindi rin perpekto / may mga depekto rin
examples.why: "magiging may depekto" is a stiff literal chain (future copula + existential) that no native technical writer would produce; it also slightly shifts "imperfect" toward "defective". Also loses the emphatic "themselves".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the three plan bullets (Premium/Open = "real-time na paggamit sa nakalipas na 28 araw (rolling)", Pay-As-You-Go = "mula nang likhain ang instance", Flex = "mula sa simula ng kontrata") each match the source exactly, nothing is inverted, softened, or invented, and the informal register holds with no po/opo. What a native technical editor would still change is phrasing, not meaning: "kung gaano na kagamit ang isang instance" (line 13) uses a non-idiomatic ka- form of "gamit" where a Tagalog writer would say "kung gaano na nagamit" or "kung gaano karami ang nagamit ng instance"; "Anumang oras, makikita mo..." (line 9) drops the linker and reads as a calque of "At any time," where "Kahit kailan" or "Sa anumang oras" is natural; and "Nag-uulat ang Instance usage ng iba't ibang halaga" (line 15) both calques "reports" and shifts the source's "a different value" into a plural "iba't ibang halaga" — the intent survives, but "Nagpapakita ang Instance usage ng magkaibang halaga" would read as written rather than translated. No misleading content; these are naturalness slips only.

examples.source: To determine how much an instance has been used
examples.translation: Para malaman kung gaano na kagamit ang isang instance
examples.suggested: Para malaman kung gaano na nagamit ang isang instance
examples.why: "kagamit" is not an idiomatic ka- adjective form of "gamit"; a native technical writer would use the completed-aspect verb "nagamit" (or "kung gaano karami ang nagamit"). Meaning is still recoverable, so this is stylistic, not misleading.

examples.source: At any time, you can see how much cost has been incurred by workloads associated with an instance.
examples.translation: Anumang oras, makikita mo kung magkano na ang nagastos ng mga workload na nauugnay sa isang instance.
examples.suggested: Kahit kailan, makikita mo kung magkano na ang nagastos ng mga workload na nauugnay sa isang instance.
examples.why: Fronting a bare "Anumang oras," mirrors English "At any time," word-for-word; Tagalog wants "Kahit kailan" or "Sa anumang oras". Grammatical but reads as translated.

examples.source: **Instance usage** reports a different value, depending on the type of plan the instance is associated with:
examples.translation: Nag-uulat ang **Instance usage** ng iba't ibang halaga, depende sa uri ng plano na nauugnay sa instance:
examples.suggested: Nagpapakita ang **Instance usage** ng magkaibang halaga, depende sa uri ng plano na nauugnay sa instance:
examples.why: "Nag-uulat" is a literal carry-over of "reports" (a UI field displays, it does not file a report), and "iba't ibang halaga" reads as "various values" where the source means "a different value per plan type". The bullets that follow disambiguate it, so no learner is misled — but the sentence is a calque.
